The most horrible thing has happened! Don Jockface, a black bubblegum stole FaYoh's gum-machine. FaYoh, a green gum, used it as storage for his stars. No one actually knows what stars are good for, but gums sure enjoy collecting them. Don Jockface had no interest in the starts though. He just wanted to search for lost coins in the machine. So the black gum carried the machine to the top of his tower, where he thought he could work undisturbed.  

FaYoh must, of course, get his bubblegum-machine back. But that's not all! Don Jockface carried the machine carelessly and dropped stars everywhere in the big tower. Before gum-fighting with Don, FaYoh must find the lost stars!

211247.overview:
Amidar is a 1982 arcade game by Konami that is now converted for the Amiga 500. This is an attempted 1:1 port for Amiga 500,  it requires 1MB memory
 

FEATURES:
- original visual & sounds
- faithful enemy behaviour & speed & increasing difficulty
- 50 frames per second (PAL) even on a 68000 A500
- all levels & bonus levels
- original intro
- joystick controlled (port 1) or keyboard controls (arrows + space)
- can run directly from shell or from whdload (fast machines/complex configurations)
 

CONTROLS:
- joystick directions/arrows: move player
- space/fire button: start game
- P/second button: pause
- F10 (or quitkey): quit (and save scores)
 

HOW TO PLAY:
- avoid enemies
- eat all dots (odd levels) to complete level
- paint all zones (even levels) to complete level. You cannot start painting from an unpainted zone
- if cornered use jump to get past the enemies
- fill all 4 corner regions to get a temporary "power state" where you can kill the enemies
- after a while, the white thief (aka tracer) will start following you. Don't wait too long!
 

CREDITS:
- Jean-Francois Fabre (aka jotd): code and gfx/sfx conversion
- Andrzej Dobrowolski (aka no9): music/sfx conversion
- Frank Wille (aka phx): sfx/module player
- meynaf: random routine
- eab forum: useful advice & support
- Superjustinbros: sprite rips https://www.spriters-resource.com/arcade/amidar
- konami: original game :)
  

Experience this recreated 1982 arcade game
Amidar500 is a free ROM for the Amiga 500 gaming console, developed by user jotd666. In this faithful 1:1 port of the 1982 arcade game, you get to move around a fixed rectilinear stage of varying sizes and divisions, with the goal being to visit all spots of the grid. Amidar500 is one of the first games in the “grid capture” subgenre of maze puzzles, together with Pac-Man 256 or Santa’s Rats Issue. Not only do you have to visit all spots of the stage but you also have to survive by evading all enemies on-screen. 
 

Revisit a genre classic!. As a ROM file in the Amiga Disk File (ADF) format, Amidar500 doesn’t run on its own. You’ll need either an actual Amiga 500 console or a supported emulator like FS-UAE or WinUAE. Similarly, you can use the Amiga Explorer to interface an Amiga system to a PC. It’s not a troublesome requirement since the emulators are free and helps in the faithful recreation of the 1982 game.
 

Like Pac-Man, there are different enemies in the game that use different movement patterns to create a challenging gameplay experience. As you progress, more varied enemy compositions try to prevent you from completing your quest. Aside from the enemies, the game also gets increasingly hard because of its increasing gameplay speed. To balance it out, you can jump past enemies and there are various power-ups available to help you.
 

Of course, as an old video game, it also has no progress-saving mechanism. When you die, you start all over again. You can slowly adapt to the game difficulty, though.

211267.overview: This game pays homage to Sylvester Stallone's movie,First Blood. In it you have five levels where you fight baddies with your "Rambo knife", hop over objects and pick up ham to replenish your health.

211270.overview: Simply try to fly the heli safely to the exit without crashing into any walls or enemies. Save your bullets and bloodalc value for getting extra-bonus points at the end of each level. Collected beer bottles can be used by holding fire button. Small collisions means you lose bloodalc, longer collisions spells instant death!

211271.overview: A Platforming game game released at Retrokomp/Loadererror Retroparty 2015, it is an unofficial port of the ZX\C64 game by RetroSouls. Alter Ego is an action puzzle platformer. In this game, you control a hero and his phantom 'alter ego' that mirrors all your moves (either horizontally or vertically) from across the screen. You can switch between the hero and his alter ego a limited number of times in each level, in order to avoid enemies and reach inaccessible places. The aim of the game is to collect all purple and green boxes which can be picked up by a hero or his phantom respectively.

211276.overview:
After suffering bullying at his high school, Daniel receives karate classes.
Once you have learned the movements, you decide to sign up for the valley karate tournament. As Daniel you will have to face all the members of the Cobra kai in the tournament and thus win the Valley tournament. In the Valley tournament mode, you can play two players in a classic match up. In the Free Tournament mode, you can play with your friends and face them to win the tournament, in this mode with up to 8 players.

211460.overview: An entry into the itch.io 2018 Seven Day First Person Shooter Jam, coded entirely between the 20th and 27th of October. The game is set in a fictional 2004,four years after the horrific events of Y2K, where appliances rule the world and only those who shunned them are free from their tyranny. Eventually, the mechano men come for your farm on the edge of Philadelphia. Use your goodly shotgun and your pitchfork to take out the tech terrors, mayhaps you'll find more weapons along the way.

211465.overview: The heavy cruiser Grant has become infeste4d by a horde of aliens that have no tolerance of humans. They have killed all crew members on board and we can no longer ignore their threat to our space ways. For this reason the aliens must be exterminated. It is your task to enter the heavy cruiser 'Grant' and destroy all life left aboard. This is a fast, fun crosshairs shooter from Craig Burfitt.

211523.overview:
Here we are with another game.
This time you will face evil Amigans Empire and their treacherous leader Great Miner as Captain Tramiel - brave and cunning commodore of Atarenium Falcon. Prototype space vessel with built-in powerful processing unit - Atari Falcon powered by eco pea-coal.
Well... at least you will try to reclaim as much coal as you can get.  Coal, that was stolen from Atari Tribe by the Amigans....

211559.overview: Somewhere in the Atlantic, at an offshore oil rig, a wreck is found. You decide to look for valuable salvage in the wreckage and make your way to the spot with a rented research sub to explore the murky depths in this point and click adventure.

211560.overview: A French point and click adventure game made by with code by Sylvain Martinez (Sa Majesté) and music and graphics by Eric Cubizolle (Titan).

211814.overview: A clone of Total Wormage. Being such big fans of WORMS, Finnish developers, Naamahaukat got permission to use some of the samples from Team 17's game for their clone.

211818.overview: Surprisingly a  truly playable fighting game, if you can look past the shabby graphics and unreliable collision detection. Still a laugh and a fun game for two.

211849.overview: A scrolling multi-directional shooter. We will begin our adventure aboard a plane in a kind of horizontal shoot'em up section, where you will simply have to avoid toxic clouds until you reach the boss at the end of the picture, when finally we will also begin to shoot a bit. Once off the plane, we will face the second action-platform matrix scenario.

211878.overview: Astro Blox is an adaptation of Soko-Ban. The aim for the player is to place boxes in the designated places. There are lots of new ideas that change the Soko-Ban aspect. Some fields create inversions which either help or make the task much more difficult.

211883.overview: 30 levels of frustrating fun! Collect all the keys and then exit via the door. Spiders will kill you if you are caught adjacent to them. Spiders will explode if they can no longer move. Snakes will spit deadly poison if you are in their line of site. Be quick or the traps will get you, but they can be blocked with boulders. Collect gems for extra points and extra lives.

211919.overview:
The Age of Rock is an updated version of Blasteris, a game by the same author from 1988.  Full version is available on cover disk of Amiga Format issue #107 and #129 where it was described as inverse Tetris with guns.

Originally a shareware game, it later got released into the public domain.

211920.overview:
Alehop seems to incorporate elements from both Clowns and Breakout. Keep a clown in the air by catching him on the other end of the see-saw and rocket them into the blocks above. Knock out all the blocks to move on to the next round. Originally presented in Retromania 2017 videogame programming contest.

The game was created for the Retromania 2017 Compo,

211921.overview: A Pong\Arkanoid style game created by Christian Kargl in 1999.

211922.overview: Spoof game based on the popular Teletubbies BBC TV programme. In this cross-hairs shooter you can get out your built-up Teletubby aggression. Time for Tubby Bye-Bye!!

211923.overview: The sequel to Armchair Assassin (The T.V. Chubbies in...). A highly entertaining murder simulator. Cute sprites burst from a wooden crate and run aimlessly in all directions. You move a crosshair and shoot at them with an arsenal of weapons and an endless amount of ammunition. Soon the screen is filled with blood, bones, and craters. You can change the music, the sounds, and even the sprites.

211924.overview: Released at the Evoke-Demoparty in August 2013. Asgard Met Vikings is an arcade style game where you (optionally joined by a friend) must catch falling bottles of mead that Odin is generously dropping from the sky whilst avoiding and/or battering the endless hordes of Goblins trying to nab your booze. Should any green skinned thieves get too close and you'll get hit and start to flash - and by that I mean actually visibly flash, not disrobe and display your Viking family jewels.

211987.overview:
An Unofficial  port of BeatSaber to the Commodore Amiga.
This is (clearly) not an exact clone of Beatsaber. It is only meant for fun and becouse it was possible to do! 
Any Song can be easily converted into the program. The converter and the Amos source code are also inclouded in the RAR file.

212119.overview: The classic Tetris game in Axel's salsa. For a long time, 'Axel Software' had been eager to make their own version of one of the classics of all time; this desire has now materialized in this new publication!  I am confident that our admirers of our previous works (and also the new ones) will appreciate the commitment always lavished in our projects, and the desire to make them more and more interesting, including this last splinter of creativity.

212130.overview: A 2D side-view shooter, written with Backbone by Thomas R. Grant. Take out the soldiers, helicopters and tanks. Pick up health where you can. Knock the baddies out of the armory. Has moments of platform action against enemy Daleks.

212170.overview:
Aggression was to be a horizontally scrolling shooter with ray traced graphics and up to 512 colours on screen at once.

There was to be full screen multilayer scrolling and very large sprites making use of every clock cycle the Amiga had to offer.

212171.overview: AmiBOX is a logic game where we have to connect all elements together in one network. On each board is one transmitter and several receivers which we have to connect to it. Each element can be rotated in two direction, left and right. To complete the level we have to connect all receivers with the transmitter using all the elements on the screen. Each board has a time limit and after it the game ends.

212172.overview: Push the ice-blocks to extinguish the walking fires. Pickup the bonus goodies if you can. And don't play with fire because you are extremely flammable. There is a timer, if things get too hot it will time out.

212258.overview: A nice looking space invaders for the Amiga that gives you the feel of the arcade machine experience.

212302.overview: You are the lone defender of the great interplanetary starship AMOS and have to resist a surprise attack from an alien race intent on the destruction of the whole Amos race. Attacking ships are loaded with explosives and try to evade your fire to make kamikaze attacks on your base ship. It is believed they will abandon their attempt if you can destroy 250 of their number, but the more you destroy, the more persistent they become! They will send faster ships and try to target you for explosives instead of the base ship. Look out for rotating mines, if you get too close you'll be cosmic dust.

212372.overview: An old idea in 3D mode where you cn swivel 360 degrees, track up and down, anticipate and try to shoot down attacking jets with missiles.

212373.overview: An action game created with Blitz Basic by Dreamsoft purporting to allow you to let play a mixture of  Breaker, Football or Pinball. All these are bat and ball games in the vein of Arkanoid with a sports themed twist.

212378.overview: A block pushing, action game written in Blitz Basic 2 by Gareth Robinson in 1995.

212380.overview: An automotive duel which takes place between two cars whizzing around a top-down viewed track. The winner is the first to either complete a set number of laps or to blast their opponent to more pieces than a warehouse full of jigsaw puzzles. Includes a course designer.

212381.overview: A FlappyBird clone for the Amiga 1200 computer, made by Dean Hand and released in 2017.

212382.overview: A game from Assassins CD 4, an overly complicated front end for a worm\Tron style game with some added features like customizable maps, caging your opponent and some interesting devices that can impact play. You can even modify each user to have different amounts of lives, jumps, teleports, breakthroughs and the aforementioned cages.

212383.overview: Based on 1998 "Homer Simpson in Russia" for ZX-Spectrum, the adventure game is a top down view adventure game where you need to find the object to help you solve the problems.

212384.overview: A version of the classic board game for up to 4 players. Players get 9 ships to arrange on the game board and the game proceeds by otherwise normal rules. This homebrew game by Bryan stu and Bill was not released to the public domain.

212398.overview: A clone of the arcade classic, Anteater for the Commodore Amiga. It was developed by Andy Chandler and released into the public domain in 1994.

212416.overview: A game of Black Jack written in AMOS BASIC 1.2 by Peter Craven, released in July 1991 and tested on the Amiga 2000 and Amiga 500. Choose between one and two players or play against the computer. Choose number of card desks to use to practice counting cards or make things extremely random.

212680.overview: A Licenseware puzzle game released by Amivision in 1993, bundled with another puzzle game, by the name of Spectra.

212683.overview: A Blitz basic Arkanoid clone with gravity and HAM mode GFX by Uffe Jakobsen in 1999. You are a downright annoying kid! As such, you have a fondness for braking stuff. And that makes your parents very ANOID. Be very annoying and we will capture you in the 5 most annoying kids!

212686.overview: Welcome to the Light Cycle battle arena where you can go head-to-head with a friend or foe!

212842.overview: Something like Atomix or Atomino but with more items and great music, by Harald Muller\Meuller. It is a German language puzzle game by Harald Muller\Mueller. On each level, you are given a couple of atoms, and your task is to arrange them into a specific molecule.

212851.overview: A four-player board game, somewhat like Sorry! written by Harald Mueller\Muller and released to Public Domain in 1995.

212856.overview: Advanced Laser Chess is a two-player strategy game. It's a more complex version of Laser Chess by the same author and adds more pieces. A 15 x 11 board with a randomly appearing displacement device at its center is the playfield. Pieces on top of the device disappear and reappear when the device is no longer visible. All pieces have unique capabilities with the diamond-shaped piece being the king, whose capture brings the end of the game, as does him being hit by a laser. Published in COMPUTE'.'s Amiga Resource Disk and on the Italian Amiga Magazine 07 disk.

212914.overview:
Africa is a strategy game where the world powers (played by up to five human or CPU players) compete for dominance in southern Africa. It is based on a 1977 board game by World Wide Wargames (3W).

The game takes place on a hexagonal map of sub-Saharan Africa, with the spheres of influence indicated by different colors. Hexagons with a thick white outline are cities, which serve as recruiting sites and bastions for armies.

Each round begins by letting each player spend his allotted money on monetary support to his client states, destabilization of enemy clients, sending in an intervention force, recruiting juntas or rebel leaders, and building stability in client states.

During the round, each player places new armies (including rebel armies in enemy states), moves them, and attacks opposing factions. Unless the force is overwhelming, the winner is decided by a throw of dice, and the (surviving) loser backs off into his own territory. If a defeated army has no retreat route, it is eliminated.

Though the game by default takes place during the cold war, there is an option to use colonial names for states and cities instead.

212915.overview: A fun and colorful little Space Invaders clone.

212969.overview: The Amiga version of 4096 is essentially a clone of the original 2048 game on mobile devices but twice as difficult! Created by Coagulus n 2014.

213590.overview:
This is another Tetris variation with some updated ideas. First there is a new object, a drop which fills five free fields in the playfield using a special algorithm. Then there is an energy bar ,which you can increase by pulling the stick down and decrement by pressing the joystick up. Meaning, the falling speed of the object is controlled by the joystick so you have very granular control of the speed at all times, as long as you have sufficient energy to control it. Finally, in two player mode when one side gets a line cleared, the other the opponent loses a field. There are 3 difficulty levels. Firing on your joystick rotates the shape. There is also a field showing the next shape up in the queue.  
 
If the game play is too fast, press H to halve the speed of the game, however, this will also halve the amount of points gained.

213591.overview:
Amigoids is a one or two player Asteroids game.

It has three game modes: single player; two players; one player with two ships. There is a high score table, joystick support and extra ships are granted for every 10,000 points scored. You start in a small Space Ship in the center of the screen, you are equipped with bullets, and your aim is to shoot the asteroids along with any flying saucers which appear throughout each level

You can move around the screen slowly or even at speed, But you must not collide with the asteroids or even the flying saucers, as this will cost you a life, The aim is to clear the level of the asteroids by shooting them, when they are hit, they gradually split into smaller and smaller pieces, which fly off in different directions, again you hit these, and they get smaller and smaller, until you hit the last piece which then disappears off screen, at this point you have completed hitting that asteroid

There are many asteroids per level of course, which will start at random positions, and float aimlessly around the screen in no general direction while you are aiming for them

213654.overview: A 2D Puzzle game by the prolific Harald Müller published in 1995. Use your mouse to press the button on a section of 4 squares, which flips the way the colors are arranged in an attempt to turn all the colors the same, a tricky proposition!

213655.overview: A BattleMech arena style fighting game. Use your shields and power up your lasers, cannons and missiles to take your your enemy at close range. Rock'em Sock'em robots but with missiles and shields.

213656.overview: Atomic Tetris for Amiga is a two player Tetris game ported from the DOS game which was originally created by Jared Tarbell , it is not meant to be played by one player vs the computer. The game is played side by side with both players sharing the keyboard. It is basically plays the same as standard Tetris, blocks fall, lines across the screen must be completed to score points etc. There is, however a twist in that there are power bricks, called Specials within the game, which, when included in a completed line, can cause the opponent problems. There are thirteen Specials in the game and their effects range from clearing the screen, switching the screens over, randomizing the opponents screen to changing all the opponents bricks into small dots making them hard to see.

213657.overview: A 2D top-down, turn based war game set in the period of the Napoleonic wars, the game was created by Jeff A. Jones of Cornerstone Software and released in 1989.

213658.overview:
This war game takes it's name from Allied actions during the second World War. Operation Avalanche was the landing of Allied forces on the west coast of mainland Italy in 1943. Accordingly, this is the scenario the game uses. The computer can be set to control either the Allied, German, or no side, and various additional settings with respect to historical circumstances (for example the loyalty of Italian forces to each side) can be made.

The main game takes place on a single, scrolling map. Units are represented by icons with no single scale (for instance, a tank icon can represent a division as well as a brigade). The gameplay structure itself consists of various phases, such as air (reconnaissance and attacks), order (for e.g. movement actions) and combat. The latter is used to calculate the results of engagements.

213762.overview: In near future, thrilling discovery was made. The inevitable invasion comes to the cradle of humanity. Researches shows that it can be stopped only by the specially crafted technology. There is not much time to contact. Only ten effective fighters will be constructed in time. Humanity need to send only the best pilots. Jump behind the simulator rudders. Be in the elite ten and save humanity from invasion.

214049.overview: Your mission is simple: stop the invasion of the aliens and blast them! Alien Blaster is a classic 2D shoot 'em up featuring lots of different weapons, special items, aliens to blast and a big bad boss. It supports both a single player mode and a cooperative two player mode for two persons playing on one computer.

214413.overview:
Back in 1985, the first Amiga 1000 computers came with the ABasiC programming language by Metacomco. Unfortunately ABasiC does not work under Kickstart 2.0 (V36) and later, but can be patched to fix the problem. David Addison wrote some excellent games in ABasiC including Amiga Othello, written in 1986. 

The David Addison games originally appeared on Fred Fish disks 28. Amiga Othello is an implementation of the board game of the same name. Players take turns placing tokens on the board, tokens that are surrounded by two tokens of another color change color. When the board is full, the player with the most tokens of their color on the board wins the game.

214517.overview: Robbo is a cross between Boulder Dash and Sokoban that has no sound or music as creatd by Robert Szacki of RNS Vision, this version also incorporates elements of Chips Challenge.

214776.overview:
A single player power casino game by Đorđe Vulović and Igor Slijepčević of the Alpha Production Team, released in Noverber 1992. 

Alfa Poker was created in the Workbench 2.0 environment (that is, embossed gadgets and all those little things that make life more beautiful) and the first thing that catches your eye is the wonderful graphic design. Mouse or keyboard can be used equally well.

214777.overview: This is Rubik's cube for classic PAL Amiga, a later version had NTSC support. Written in Amos Professional 2.0, game download contains source code.

214778.overview: Released in English and eventually in Polish, this solitaire game was created by David W. Meny and Albert Penello and released in 1991. An Amiga implementation of the "Klondike" solitaire with a totally mouse-driven, OS-friendly interface. There are settings for if the game should keep times, if the deck should be flipped one or three cards at a time, how many times one may flip through the deck, an undo function and a cheat function to glimpse through a stack. There are six decks to choose from, including one with the Amiga checkmark and one with a Batman theme.

214780.overview: A one or two player shooter game by Amiga Live, released as a public domain game in 1990.

214781.overview: AmiGo was one of the first Go programs publicly available with source code. It is based on a Pascal program written by Stoney Ballard in 1983 and posted to USENET and was ported to C and the Amiga by Todd R. Johnson in 1989. Multiple updates and releases have been made to this game over the years with v6.3 being released in

214788.overview: An Amiga bridge playing program. You play with a computer partner against two computer opponents. It includes an online Bridge tutorial. A hint mode is available in all situations.

214813.overview: Released as "almost finished", this role playing game by Daniel Wienzek can be considered a demo. The author got frustrated after changing the graphics for additional support but the maps didn't update properly and Daniel was done with it and rage-published it in 1997 with a plea that someone help him fix the maps.

214891.overview: A one or two player beach volleyball game by tukinem with graphics by Don Rafito and released in 2022 and has already had some code revisions for faster code and better customization in the latest version.

214896.overview: 'Adam is me' is a conversion of the puzzle game, Baba Is You for the Amiga: by moving and joining tiles on the playing field, on which nouns and verbs are noted, the rules of the respective level are changed in such a way that the game character can finish the section.

214956.overview:
Manic and chaotic fun containing 55 kick ass blasting rooms, lots of enemies to fight, an awesome soundtrack, the ability to strafe and treasure to collect. Fast paced, top down, action/rpg! Discover a magical AGA title, unlike any other!  The holy island of Alarcity has been invaded by an unknown army seeking it's secrets. Assume the role of 'Algernon', a mysterious entity from a different plane, summoned (unwillingly) on the island and caught into the conflict.

Face dangerous enemies and hunt the powers of the Gods in an epic journey across the land! Find treasures, gain experience and become the ultimate weapon!

215043.overview: A from scratch homebrew version of Alien Storm in AMOS. To compensate for AMOS' famous slowness it was downsized to a portion of the screen as though it were being played on a Game Gear handheld, which resolved much of the slowness and scrolling issues. It remains in an unfinished but playable state up to the Gilling Monster.

215066.overview: There you are, on a dusty road in the middle of the Hoimon desert and your enemies are right at your heels. It has been two days since you escaped from the captivity of the orcs and their allies. Your destination is the city of Spannenberg. You will be safe there and catch your breath. It sis still a long way to Newlake, but soon you will be reunited with your friends.  ...and then the orc's barbaric slavery will be put to an end.

215096.overview: In this Game and Watch style game by Carlos Peris you must get the key, avoid the nasties and make your way to the top of the level safely. It is based on the gameplay of Game & Watch: Donkey Kong II.

215097.overview: "Redpill Racing" is a top-down-view racer, which was created bt Hyabde3050 in 2017 using the Game Construction Kit Redpill.

215118.overview: King Triton will not let Freddy Fish marry his beautiful daughter Ariel until Freddy can afford the lifestyle a princess like her deserves. So Freddy begins an aquatic adventure to collect gold bars from the bottom of the ocean. You have to carry each bar individually up to the boat on the surface. In each of the sixteen levels, a host of enemies chase you. It is a simple and colorful game with lots of art assets lifted from James Pond. Chris Sorrell even gets a cheeky special thanks in the credits.

215361.overview:
Agricola is a neat platformer featuring a farmer called Freddy. It as created by Alce programmers Baldassare Dante Profeta, gfx Giuseppe Stassi, Ignazio Stagnitta and sound by Filippo Vela.

There are two versions of Agricola available for download. The ADF is an early demo with a menu and credits screen.

The second version is an archive of files which can be run from hard disk. It seems to be a later release than the ADF demo. Run the appropriate file (Agricola_L1 for level 1, for example) to launch each level. The game was cancelled and while it was more than 80% done, when shopped around, it was never picked up for release by any of those companies looking.

215381.overview: Tennis Champs is a 1995 Tennis Game from Mental Image, followed the same year by the game Super Tennis Champs. It was pre-released under the name of  Arcade Sports Tennis. Coded in AMOS by the excellently named Elton and Elliot Bird, manages to be better than all of them by taking its inspiration from the world of consoles and simply being a lot of fun. A clever and intuitive control system allows all manner of shots to be played with a one-button joystick. There are four different playing surfaces and a variety of players to choose from, and even a tournament mode.

215382.overview: Angst is an first person 3D shooter game, developed by Rave Software and published by DEM Software, which was released in Europe in 1995. The pre-release/prototype version was called Paranoia.

215471.overview: Thalamus secured the license for this arcade/management footy sim after Arsenal won the English Premier League in 1991-92. Scheduled for release in Sept/Oct '92 with the inclusion of an official Arsenal souvenir (whoopie cushion perhaps??!!), the game never materialised on any platform due to Thalamus' financial woes which forced them into receivership in 1993. No doubt ARSENAL FC's failure to hit store shelves was a terrible disappointment to Man Utd fans and other English Premier League club fans the world over!

215475.overview:
Atrophy is an unrealesed shoot'em up game.

The game began life as ATROPHY in 1995 and was originally scheduled for release on A1200/4000 (disk/CD) and CD32 by Guildhall in late 1995. Bitter internal fighting within the development team regarding game design (predominantly gfx and music) and up-front royalty payments resulted in the game's release being continually delayed. Reportedly, central to the internal fighting was team coder Frank Tout (The Art/LSd!)

215500.overview: You must shoot the Alien in the head as many times as possible until its eventual demise and you've won. The game is played in a third person in the style of Quake or Doom. Indeed some graphics from Quake are present in the current build brought to us by mastaszek in 2019, first alphas released in 2017.

216758.overview: A public domain release from The Assassins that contained Jumping Jack, Technoball and Zillo. These compilations were sold by mail order through a number of suppliers of public domain software who would usually assign their own catalogue number, so it is not uncommon to find the same compilation on offer from multiple suppliers in the same magazine, usually for a fairly nominal fee above the cost of the disk and copying labor.

217107.overview:
The Amiga Spiele 1 is a Markt & Technik compilation of three low-budget games developed in Germany that were never released elsewhere. The following games are included:

1) Wikinger

As the name suggests, Wikinger is a strategical conquest game taking place in Northern Europe around 900 A.D.. The initial choice to be made is how many human players shall participate, the number ranges from five people down to zero with the latter option boiling down to watching five computer-controlled players battle it out. Of course, there are precisely five nations to choose from that are in desperate need of a leader, namely Iceland, England, Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. As the goal of the game is to conquer as much land as possible, Iceland is, for geographical reasons, by far the hardest nation to succeed with, where Denmark is the easiest.

Every nation starts the game with one single staging post that controls 10 villages. From this point forward, the most important thing is to raise some viking armies to conquer new lands which will increase the people count and, thus, the player's income. Not later than the first meeting with foreign armies, the player should have built up a working economy that will exemplary enable him to equip his armies with weaponry and boating, build new staging posts that will harden his defense, or buy additional wheat to compensate for bad harvests. The latter combined with a low tax rate will significantly increase the young nation's head count.

2) Gölzy's Bliff (aka Bliff)

Bliff is a simple billiard adaption with one cue ball, one other ball and one pocket. Goal of the game is to pot the other ball using the cue ball which gives the single player mode a decent feeling of mini golf, a feat also amplified by the different loadable tables that come with the game. There is a two player hot-seat mode, too, where every player has to pot the other player's ball. Furthermore, the player can design his own tables and save them to disc, thus being able to share them with fellow players.

3) Quadriga

Quadriga is a computer adaption of the popular strategy game Connect Four. Two players are to assign stones to a 7x7 board with each player's goal of connecting four of them horizontally, vertically or diagonally, while hindering the other player in doing so. The game can be played by one or two human players with the artificial intelligence of the possible computer player coming with five different IQ's. It is even possible to let two computer players battle it out, testing whether the higher difficulty levels really play better than the lower ones in the process.
 
Also known as Amiga Software Extra Nr. 3 Spiele.

217108.overview:
It is the unimaginably distant year 2009. You are Nick Vrenna, falsely locked inside a high security prison. The genetic experiments conducted in the prison, combined with a full-scale riot that took place recently, caused all guards and inmates to be transformed into insane, aggressive mutants. Your job is to escape while stopping the genetic plague from transforming the whole world.

Abuse is a side-scrolling platformer with a lot of shooting. It's a nonlinear game, as the levels often have a few exits that lead to different areas. Your character is a cyborg equipped with various weapons; initially, you only have a weak laser rifle with unlimited ammo, but you can find more powerful guns later on, such as grenade launchers, flamethrowers or lightsabers. You move through a building complex, fighting any enemies you might encounter on the way. The enemies are mostly the mutants, but also the defense systems (such as stationary missile launchers).

While you move with the keyboard, you can aim with your mouse, so you can shoot at any angle no matter what direction you are running. On your way, you'll find elevators, teleporters, cracked walls that can be destroyed and more.

Apart from ammo and health, you can also find upgrades which have a number of beneficial effect - increasing your running speed, for example.

217147.overview:
Released free with other Team 17 games, this full version of Apache and demo of Overdrive was first released in 1993. It was created by the team of David J. Broadhurst, Haydn Dalton and music by Allister Brimble (The Demon). 

Apache is a Choplifter/Fort Apocalypse type scrolling horizontal helicopter shooter, while Overdrive is a very good overhead racing game. 

Apache was never released separately.

217258.overview:
A classic vertical shoot em up made by DarkGiver 

for the Amiga Blitz Basic Game Jam

You're piloting an unidentified strong and well armed turboprop plane with swiss colours (but who looks like a modernized F6F Hellcat...) in an alternate history world.

217265.overview: This is a port of Icy Tower written in Blitz Basic 2 for Amiga.

218059.overview: This program presents a variety of deductive reasoning puzzle stories that encourage students to think logically, read carefully, and comprehend material read. Through critical reading and the process of elimination, strategies for problem solving are developed. If you can complete logic problems correctly, a letter of a randomly selected password will be revealed. Problems consist of a reading passage presenting a problem for Genlock Holmes to solve and one or more logic grids to fill in. You may look back to the story passage while solving the logic grids. Reading passages are intriguing, and will fascinate even the reluctant reader. There are 20 story exercises in all. Students must consider implications, make inferences, and draw conclusions. Information must be "processed", not merely recalled.

218085.overview:
A game modeled on Wood Block Puzzle.
Minimal requirements: Amiga 500.

218698.overview: This is a sokoban clone game with some extra features. The game contains 34 levels and is a sequel to Astro Box.

219062.overview: Athanor 2 not only features a typical 80's style North, South, East command interface of adventure games of old, but unlike the first game which we also enjoyed, it features full mouse control, enriched dialogues, different phases of gameplay, throughout multiple locations through 4 worlds, full 256 colours, extra sounds and much much more all for your Amiga 1200 and above. So yes certainly a game that if you get the chance to buy it, you'll be pleased to have it in your collection!

219082.overview: MineSweeper (final release) for any Amiga. Game is system-friendly and working on kickstart 1.3 and laters. It's my first game on system Intuition Screen.

219291.overview: A homebrew Yahtzee style dice game for 2 to 9 players made by Alpha Production Team and released in 1992.

219376.overview: Align sets of 5 or more colored balls in lines to score. the bigger the lines, the more you score. Game ends when the field is full.

275394.overview:
Adidas Championship Football is a soccer game with 24 national teams. The only playing mode is a championship which mimics the World Cup with randomly drawn groups. A second player can control a second team.

The playing perspective is top-down with a scrolling field. The control method is an expanded dribbling method known from the Kick Off series. To make a shot, the player needs to hold down the button for a certain amount of time (this determines the power of the shot) and only then play the ball. The angle can be changed by tapping the button.

418350.overview: An arcade style underground mining game created by Last Minute Creations and ranked 2nd in Retrokomp 2018 game development contest. Each level provides a dollar value goal that must be met within the time limit to move on to the next. The game is set in a Communist theme. You have been sent to this facility by the decision of Ministry of Mining and Fossile Fuels. The outpost is small but we believe not yet fully explored and examined. As you know, development of our great Democratic Peoples Republic requires significant expenditures in the sector of heavy industry. Industry that will astound and amaze with its creations not only imperialist in the West but the whole world. Industry that is so important for our great Army that protects our Motherland and helps to liberate more and more nations from the imperial and capitalist occupant.

418430.overview: A one or two player Shareware shooter from Paul Nordovics written in Blitz Basic. The game takes place in a number of mazes. Each player controls an alien. Energy pods appear at random positions. You have to collect 10 energy pods before your opponent. The more you collect, the more powerful your weapon becomes. If you kill opponents, they lose pods.

418622.overview: The game tries to represent the African part of 11th Paris-Dakar rally route, which in the game takes place in Tunisia, Algeria, Niger, Burkina Faso, Mali, and Senegal in 1988-1989. Controlling his(her) car in third-person 'behind the car' view, player should drive through the marked path in Sahara. When player loses his(her) way, he(she) may be in the sands alone and start to skid. In this situation he(she) may switch between 4x4 and 4x2 modes of the car. These modes have own opportunities and misses. The speed is limited to 87 in 4x4 mode and limited by car's parameters in 4x2 mode. But in 4x4 mode path marks may stop the car, while in 4x2 mode the car may knock the path parks off. Switching the gear, player may drive back and forth to avoid blocking of car either by path mark or by debris in the sand. Direction of the way is shown by compass as well as length of traversed path and volume of residuary fuel are displayed by indicators. Other drivers are present on the way during day and night, therefore they should be left behind to win in the rally. There are five stages with different visible horizons: 1) Tunis - In Salah (5726 Km); 2) Ouallene - Achegour (4353 Km); 3) Achegour - Niamey (4587 Km); 4) Ouagadougou - Bamako (4438 Km); 5) Bamako - Dakar (3622 Km). So, you have to conquer the sands of Sahara, show good time on each stage, and to be the first at the finish.

418734.overview:
A snake-game for an Amiga.


 - Single player or Two players mode (split screen)

 - 6 different worlds

 - adventure story mode

418885.overview:
Agonman is a small game inspired by a static image of Edwin Van del Heuvel (with his permission) with some modified gfx from the game Agony, except for the Owl and as a tribute to Agony/Psygnosis. It all started as an experiment, using the Zener REDPILL game maker and created in 16 colours for Amiga AGA.

Collect Psygnosis logos, avoid enemies, find the exit and destroy the final bosses, accompanied by a magnificent soundtrack by Zoltar.

420279.overview:
Go into an epic adventure in Absolute Zero, a mesmerizing puzzle platformer where you are Corben, a courageous explorer, on a dangerous quest to 
save our frozen world. As Corben, you must collect the batteries to activate the climate reactors, to unleash the elements and restore balance before 
it's too late.

420570.overview: A Redpill based shooter game from TechniMan and FireBoy of Custom Real Amigas Never Emulated, released in 2018.

420578.overview: An AMOS based text adventure created by Pedro Fernández as a Christmas gift to you and about a Christmas gift to you.  Written in AMOS Professional. Coding, digitised graphics & music by Pedro Fernández (Rockersuke); audio samples by Johan Brodd (JoBro) and infobandit.

420715.overview:
This remake of Atic Atac adds new graphics and sounds to the 1983 action-adventure title, while maintaining the same gameplay of the original.

The player controls one of three characters: a knight, a wizard, or a serf, each with unique weapons and routes through the castle. The objective is to navigate the rooms of a haunted castle, killing ghosts, and other supernatural creatures, while collecting the items necessary to open new passages, like keys and other helpful objects. The energy bar is a roasted chicken at the left side of the screen, that is slowly consumed with every hit received by the hero, until only the bones are left on the plate and the player loses one life. Trapdoors and staircases give access to other floors.

420802.overview: A game made by Graham Humphrey and Mihcael, Marco Pedrana and Jason Hill as the team named Underground Arcade. It was written in Blitz BASIC, mostly finished in 2016 and released as Public Domain. A horizontally scrolling space shooter of the usual sort with power-ups, waves of enemies, end-of-level bosses… you name it! It feature seven (count ‘em) themed levels: space, a strange alien forest, a strange alien desert, arctic, a ruined city (and not a strange alien in sight), a volcano and finally, the base (a strange alien one, naturally).

420809.overview: A demo of a Bomberman style game created by Matthew Goode in 1996. Originally meant to be an Exvania clone, but after issues trying to get joystick inputs to work properly, I switched it to a Bomberman clone. Currently it supports a single player, but a recompile could get it with two users working.

420864.overview:
A homebrew port of the Ultimate Play the Game classic where growing the best TMC possible is the sole purpose of Robbie the Robot. When insects invade his garden, he has to stop them ruining his work. He has a canister of insect repellent, a smoke-bomb and a startling streamer, each placed on walls at the side of his garden. Each will stun any particular vermin, but you will need to find out exactly what kills what.

As the plant grows, aided by the timely addition of compost bags, leaves will start to shoot outwards. The more leaves there are, the quicker it will grow (a simple incorporation of the concept of photosynthesis being boosted by having more sunlight absorbed), so don't let the bugs near it - those whose programmed movement path takes them towards an existing leaf should be your priority. Once the plant is high enough, it flowers and you move onto another level, where increasingly tough foes are on the prowl.

421002.overview:
ENFORCER demo is available on Vulcan's CD. Known as both Atmosfear and Enforcer, this is a very early version of a fake Doom clone written in AMOS. The selection of three weapons are standard; a pistol, shotgun and machine/plasma gun. Some sound and graphics, including the hand and pistol image, seem to have made a jump from Doom directly! A few monsters appear and attack from all directions.

It’s similar to Death Mask in that no real time 3D or texture mapping is involved. The first person view is created using the old Dungeon Master technique but some nifty animation makes the transition between blocks smooth. When walking forward the view bobs up and down and progresses convincingly. Similarly, turning around on the spot looks right, because the background is being scrolled horizontally to simulate the changing panorama. The bogus Doom style has its drawbacks in this case and produces a maze which is like the lines in graph paper. It’s excessively uniform and perhaps the limitations of the demo prevented further development. Vulcan would later publish Marble Eyes’ Genetic Species, so perhaps they realized the limitations of the fake style and went for the real thing instead.

421023.overview:
Having recently rediscovered some old projects, I thought I'd share the final Work-in-progress version of AMRWolf, a Texture-mapped raycasting engine writtenin a mixture of AMOSPro and assembly language.

Compared with the original demo released in 1996, this version has a couple of extra levels, a map editor and comes with full source.

421040.overview: This is a shareware mastermind-type game in which the player must work out a hidden combination of colors based on clues given by the game.  The shareware game was free to distribute, but users would need to pay in order to gain access to all features, updates and to remove nags. The game was later published in Now That's What I Call Games in 1993 for CD enabled Amiga computers by Multi Media Machine Ltd.

421051.overview: A demo game created using AMOS and Backbone by Johnny Acevedo Martin and MsMadLemon for Amiten Software in 2018. It is a single player platformer where you jump on the rats, and other denizens of the darkness, collect the crosses and stay out of the spike pits. The goal is to find the exit and leave this place.

421060.overview: The Acorn Court is a tiny text adventure developed by Todd S. Murchison for the Amiga, and released into the public domain in 1997. A small, one-location gadget game in which you must escape from a court. The game shows Inform's capability of handling multiple equal objects. A one-room gadget game involving an oak tree and an automatic tennis ball launcher. Very short and plotless but nicely implemented.

421062.overview: An emulated conversion of the classic game using the Frotz command interpreter, Adventureland is the first of Scott Adams' text adventures. Using simple two word commands you explore an enchanted world, solve puzzles and try to recover 13 lost treasures. The game's display is different from other adventure games like Zork: The Great Underground Empire in that the screen is divided into two "windows": the room description, exits, and items appear on the top part of the screen, and you enter commands on the bottom of the screen.

421063.overview: A shareware helicopter shooter. You have unlimited missiles and very limited wipeouts which will take out all enemies on the screen. There are 6 levels of firepower. Every time your helicopter is destroyed, you lose one. There are also several power ups giving extra wipeouts, one that gives extra lives and one to up your firepower.

421064.overview: A somewhat unfinished shareware platformer release from BSY Software, there was a demo that only took you to level three, a full version is reported to exist. Collect the cash and items and avoid the baddies. Some levels require you to get a set level of money to purchase items.

421193.overview:
Remake of the original Atari 8-bit version (The music is however a remix of the C64 version's music):. Like a combination of Trailblazer and an often-seen demoscene effect, you fall down a tube, landing on each square progressively in a rhythmic manner. Landing on certain tiles will have certain effects, such as making the screen quake, decreasing the brightness or forcing you to jump. Navigating the tube itself is a matter of planning ahead and compensating for your limited movement capabilities.  
 
the game would later be reworked and released under the name Jump.

421195.overview: Aztec Challenge by Cobe is based on the original Commodore 64 version, but with much upgraded graphics. Like in the original, the player must reach and explore an Aztec temple while avoiding a variety of dangerous obstacles. Each level is like a whole different game, with different challenges and different types of scrolling and exploration. The game starts with an over-the-shoulder view of the player running a gauntlet of spear-throwing natives towards a pyramid which rises on the horizon. Once this is reached, a vertically-scrolling staircase with falling rocks must be traversed, and then there are rooms to explore and deadly aquatic wildlife to avoid (among other dangers) before the game is through.

421203.overview: Backbone demo game made by Vincent Perkins in 2 hours.

421206.overview: A Yahtzee style, German language Public Domain game written in BASIC.

421423.overview: This is a text adventure game based on a dark version of the Lewis Carroll classic ! The game is in Czech with some graphics from American McGee's Alice. Excellent text game for the Amiga with a mountain of zombies and a little Alice by Crudesys from 2010.

421424.overview: An AMOS based strategy game by Mark Potter released as freeware in 1991.

421426.overview: Shoot the bad guys and NOT the good guys!! Extra points for exceptional speed. A public domain game created by Dean Prunier and released as PD in 1992.

421427.overview: A 2 player shooter which takes place in an arena. Written in AMOS by Paul Nordovics and released as shareware in 1993.

421428.overview: A one or two player freeware game created by Anthony Roberts with AMOS in 1995, where you take part as a bird and shoot other birds in the style of the game Dogfight!

421429.overview: A Qix clone created by A-Maze Design and released to PD in 1993. You just need to cut out parts of the picture, without getting hit by the monsters and objects.

421433.overview: A game preview released by Digital Technology in May 15, 1988 at Vortex 42 Computer Meeting 1988. Come for the game, stay for the music.

421435.overview: Take n the alien hordes in an arcade shoot'em up created by Jason Shallcrass and published in the May 1992 Amiga Computing Issue 48.

421475.overview: An Emerald Mine creation by Mr. B and tested by No One and the Blockheads in 1991. A.k.a. 'Mr. Mine 1'. This and the two sequels were a commercial release for Emerald Mine Club members.

421480.overview: An Emerald Mine creation by Mr. B and tested by No One and the Blockheads in 1992. Also titled  'Mr. Mine 1'. This and the prequel and one sequel were a commercial release for Emerald Mine Club members. This release has 81 caves, with caves designed by Mr. B, Caveman and Goofy.

421481.overview: A Boulder Dash style game created with the Emerald Mine Editor and first released in 1992, with updates following. Commercially released as a part of the Emerald Mine Club disk.

421990.overview: An Ultima-like game. This game contains at least four moderately-sized continents to explore. Game by Paul Falstad uses key presses instead of a parser. E.g. [ ; # and / to move around, A = attack etc.

422088.overview:
A freeware Amiga version of Nethack, a retro dungeon crawler based on Hack Lite and Nethack 2.2. With the slogan of "Plays great, less killing", Hack Lite II is part of the Hack lineage, the result of a merge of PC Hack and Amiga Hack (the latter a port of UNIX Hack 1.03), with version 2 also bringing enhancements from NetHack. The objective is to venture down a multi-level dungeon to retrieve the Amulet of Yendor and bring it back to the surface. It uses a graphical character set from the start and offers several playability enhancements such as new enemies and artifacts, while staying true to the character-based movement and keyboard commands, but also using drop-down menus and mouse clicks to identify characters or move around. There are three character sets; one with 16 colours, one with 8 colours and one using plain ASCII letters. Using a supplied program, the user can create his own character sets as well. Another included program, HackConfig, lets the user create different profiles for use with the game.

New enemies include Quantum Mechanics, Demon Lords, Princes, Liches, Golems and the Medusa. New objects include leashes, blindfolds, mirrors, stethoscopes and magic markers. You can #sit on thrones and #dip things into fountains. If things look bleak, you can #pray to the gods, as long as you don't overdo it. Spell books teach you spells, but casting them takes mental energy, and your memory of the spell fades with time.

422258.overview: Set up and run your own successful Bingo game in real life. The shareware software allows you to create flyers, betting lines, jackposts, prizes and to present it to a full house and rake in the dough. Released by Dave Brown in 1993.

422311.overview: You awake in the rain and mud with nothing to help you. You must gather tools to survive, find a way inside the church so that the vicious guard dog doesn't get you and leave it with your soul your own. The hardest part will be to leave your sins behind....literally.

422364.overview: A Frotz port of the text adventure game A Week In The Life -- An Interactive Self, created by Neil James Brown and ported to the Amiga in 1997.

422509.overview: The game was only released in Denmark in a store chain called Betafon. It was the first game that the author sold. It is an educational game with a number of simple games aiding learning.

422510.overview: A Mouse in the Dark is an educational, action game sold to schools and learning programs as licenceware starting in 1990 that encouraged critical thinking with sections like The Maze, Hidden Walls, Hidden Mouse and Hidden Walls and Mouse. You learn to navigate around obstacles that are not there and build a map in your mind.

422534.overview: A shareware quiz developed and published by Techware in 1994. Wonderful German quiz program with tons of Amiga related questions.

422552.overview: Educational program for learning chemistry. In addition to a large amount of didactic material in text and graphic form, the player has at his disposal the periodic table of elements and a set of tests. The questions have three answers, one of which is correct. After completing the tests, the score is displayed.

422558.overview: Agresor is a Polish crosshairs shooter. The game takes place on a single location. The player's task is to track down and kill all the enemies, avoiding killing any innocent civilians. A new enemy appears every few seconds. The player may select one of three available weapons: machine gun, bazooka, grenade. Targeting enemies involves moving viewfinder to the right, left, up or down and killing the bandit as fast as possible. All remaining on board enemies take energy points with every single shot. Grenade, as the most powerful weapon, kills all the characters currently present on board.

422564.overview: Afryka is an educational program that tests knowledge about Africa. The program consists of three parts, two educational parts and tests. The test includes knowledge of countries, capitals, flags, area, population, currency, climate, rivers, mountains and more.

422574.overview: A homebrew shooter from Scum Amiga Software, created with AMOS and released in 1995. Source code is included with the game. We had hoped that peaceful beings came from another planet. The mother animal came to earth and laid eggs. Then the fight began.

422587.overview: A Polish language educational geography game from Mariusz Matura, published by Atares in 1993.  The program familiarizes the user with the geopolitical situation in Asia and includes an attractive quiz testing the knowledge acquired by the program user.

422601.overview: Learn the alphabet and have fun with animation, pictures, letters and song. For users ages 4 to 7.

422605.overview: Geography Playfully is a topography practice program. Children practice their topographical knowledge in a playful way. The program is very user-friendly. You can get started right away without complicated instructions. A lot of attention has also been paid to the design.

422699.overview: A Swedish educational game from Stefan Lundberg that was released in 1990.

422701.overview: This is a preview of the adventure game ANDORA: Forest Prison made by Eric Cubizolle and Sylvain Martinez. In the final version there will be 5 areas: the forest, the village, the temple, the two others. The story is inspired by several fantastic events. The action takes place as you must discover what is at the heart of such a forest where one cannot escape. It has 64 colors. 188 wanderers per level... or 588 screens in total, 1 to 5 different languages. Ability to speak with the characters.

422704.overview: A Swedish language educational game featuring reading the clock from Stefan Lundberg and released in 1991.

422705.overview: A Swedish educational game from SPAB, released in 1991.

422706.overview: Automata is an extremely versatile, cellular automaton simulation with LOTS of settings to fiddle with, great fun!

422707.overview: An AMOS based quiz game created by Mark Venn and released in 1991. Different versions of this game exist, some PD, others shareware. The game has a built-in question\game editor for making your own quizzes. The quizzes are presented 10 questions at a time.

422708.overview: A single player horizontally scrolling shooter by Equinox created in 1990.

422709.overview:
You live in Paris, your surname is Renard and you are 26 years old. You've recently received a message from New York, together with a plane ticket and a check. "Please come urgently, I must see you. A letter is waiting for you in New York. " Who is he, what does he want from you? There is no name, no explanation, only the initials J.P.S.  
 
Choose the locations you will visit and explore the mystery while you explore the city of New York.

422750.overview: Lykkehjulet is the Danish version of the Wheel of Fortune television game show. Airing in 1988, the show was the first big American game show to be imported and just 2 years later Damo Soft put out this version of the game for the Amiga.

422752.overview: A four reel pub style fruit\slot machine. Intended to be, "...as near as possible, an exact copy of the sort of Fruit Machine you find in any snooker hall or members club. It was created with AMOS and published by Mandrin/Jawx in 1991.

422796.overview: A noir setting text adventure created by Trygve Jensen. Released on the 17-bit disk #1810 PD disk and also on the 5-disk, Adventure Pack (P). The night was as dark as a pocket, with rain coming down in sheets and only an occasional flash of lightning to perk things up a bit. Three men are coming up the elevator. When they get to your door they will kill you. Think quickly and you may live. Or hesitate and die.... again and again and again.

422798.overview: Pong at the next level, a homebrew game from Joker Developments in 1997. A game for one or two players. All things can be modified, Audio, power-ups, walls, game length and bat speed.

422801.overview: Hexagonal Tetris, so each piece has six rotations instead of just four from David Markley and Markus Wild from 1990. It was also forked under the same name by Jeff W Teague with improvements.

422803.overview: A shareware single player space invaders clone created with AMOS, coded by R. Crawley and released by Reality in 1991.

422804.overview: A Scorched Earth style two player shooter duel game from Markus Gayda of Soaring Software that came out in 1993.

422853.overview: A 2017 French language, retro, homebrew quiz game by Marksilla.

422868.overview: An Amiga based freeware Tamagotchi game where you must care and feed your sprite to keep it happy!

422892.overview: A Matter of Time is an introductory text adventure in which you must search for a lost scientist accused of murdering a fellow colleague. This missing scientist has invented a time machine, and you must travel through time in search of him. The game has a simple choose your own adventure style command system and includes full Save\Load features.

422897.overview: A two player Wheel of Fortune with voice synthesis game created by Kent Shafer in 1988, based on the TV show of the same name.

422923.overview:
The year is 2227. The powerful DDT Corporation has sent a factory ship called the Toronto to harvest minerals and resources from Albion, a newly discovered world which is supposedly barren of life but rich in resources. The space pilot Tom Driscoll is sent to take some atmospheric readings on the planet, but crash lands after an apparently accidental systems failure of his shuttle. Upon recovering from the accident he is shocked to discover that Albion is in fact a rich, life-filled world inhabited by various races with their unique cultures. It then becomes his task to explore the strange new world, helps its inhabitants, and eventually find his way back to Toronto.

Albion is a party-based role-playing game and a spiritual successor to Amber games. It features two principal exploration modes, 3D and 2D. The first-person 3D mode, similar to that of The Elder Scrolls: Arena, is used for most towns and all dungeons. The 2D mode takes place in the overworld, in smaller locations, and inside buildings, and uses a top-down perspective similar to Ultima VII: The Black Gate. Mouse or keyboard can be used to navigate the protagonists and interact with the environment.

The player controls a party of up to six characters in the game, all of which can be recruited in various locations in the game world and join the protagonist for plot-related reasons. Each character has his or her own unique fighting styles, abilities, and in some cases magic spells. Experience points are acquired by defeating enemies or solving puzzles; in addition, the player receives a set amount of training points that can be used to raise the characters' skills (such as close or ranged combat, magic, etc.). Enemies can be encountered in both 3D and 2D areas; a battle initiates when the protagonist comes into contact with an enemy. Combat is turn-based and takes place on a 2D 6x6 square grid. Topic-based dialogue system is used to obtain information about the game world, receive assignments, and advance the plot.

422932.overview:
A tie-in to the 1984 film The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai :Across the 8th Dimension, you play Dr. Banzai that ultimately tries to overcome a potentially planet-destroying bomb set by the Black Lectroids, inhabitants of Planet 10. 

The game was later converted to theoretically every platform thanks to a pair of open source tools that can be used to convert all the original Scott Adams games back to source code and then compile it to the target system. Amiga conversion was done in 2003.

423042.overview: A demo of a point and click style, visual novel version of Resident Evil for the Amiga, the full game by Aaron Holt was never finished. The demo was released in 1998.

423087.overview: A bird's eye view, single player Roguelike. It is based off of an early mainframe game and was created and published by The Software Distillery in 1987 with 12 version updates being made. The game is one of the first Roguelikes (RPG dungeon crawls with top-down or isometric graphics and a high degree of randomization; Rogue or Nethack are examples) with a wilderness and more than one dungeon. In this game, you are searching the Caverns of Larn for a cure for your daughter's strange disease. The game world is presented entirely with ASCII text characters.

423341.overview:
Author Info: Quentin D. Thompson is the pseudonym of Ravi Philip Rajkumar, a medical student from India who writes text adventures in his spare time.
 
Set in the Varicella universe in the aftermath of Primo Varicella's assassinating spree, A Stegosaur's Night Out is both an interesting followup to Adam Cadre's Varicella and an entertaining satire of the said game. The player character is...well...unusual. You're a toy. A plastic dinosaur toy. A TOY. Okay, okay, you're the plastic toy stegosaurus from Varicella, but let's not pretend that that makes it too much more appealing. I mean, come on: who really WANTS to be a toy? You'll just get picked up by some intolerable infant, kicked around, maybe have your ears chewed a bit, and then be tossed into the closet to mildew. What an intolerable existence! I wouldn't want it for my life - I don't want it in my text adventures. Rest assured, however, that this is no ordinary toy. It is a toy gifted with sentience, and possessed with a diabolical intent; namely, to assassinate the not-so-good Prince Charles of Piedmont. This is definitely the coolest toy ever. The goal of the player, then, is to make the stegosaurus' dreams come true. It shall not prove to be an easy task.

423555.overview: A text game based on the story of Asterix and Obelix, once sold in our meadows and groves in 1993, the game is supplemented with beautiful, black and white scanned images. It was created by Duel Soft.

423582.overview: Mystery Fun House is a port of the seventh entry in the original Scott Adams adventure series to the Amiga. The events of the game take place at an amusement park. The first puzzle involves figuring out how to get in past the turnstiles. Once inside, the player must solve the mystery of the place, going through a house of mirrors and so forth. Like the others in the series, the game is a text adventure with a rather basic two-word command parser. The Japanese computer versions feature graphics in addition to the text input.

423644.overview: Part of a threesome of text adventures by the veteran text adventure writer, John Wilson. this is the second game in the series, following From Out of a Dark Night Sky and preceeding The Second Night. This game was created for multiple different platforms aside from the Amiga, including the Amstrad CPC, Atari ST, C16\Plus4, C64/128, CP/M, MSX, MSX2 and the Spectrum computers.

423645.overview: A "minesweeper" game for the Amiga. Unlike most games of its kind, it runs in full-screen (though fully multitasking), uses sound effects and is (moderately) more colourful than usual. There is a "safe start" option so that one cannot hit a mine as an opening move. There are three preset minefield sizes, and a setting for custom sizes and bomb percentages. As an aid to bad losers, there is an "undo" button.

423659.overview: A single player remove the peg style board game created in 1990 by Thomas-Paul Shultz and published as a coverdisk on Amiga Action #62. Jump pegs to an empty spot to remove them and try to remove all but one!

423662.overview: The child must move a small cursor on the screen which will allow him to associate one of four proposed objects. For example the rain and the umbrella.. The child should use the cursor to associate two objects on the screen, with four objects to choose from. Developed by Vivian Peschardt and published in 1989 by Carraz Editions.

423673.overview: A single player, freeware implementation of Backgammon created by David Addison and John Everett using AmigaBASIC. You will play the light pieces and move clockwise from the upper left. To  move a piece, click on the piece to be moved and the destination point. To bear off, use the bar on the left as the destination. If you do not have a valid move, click on the dice.

423697.overview: This is a curious shareware game that plays like a multi player version of the well known game Snake, which looks and plays very similar to Červii. The game title means to Watch the Curve. Like in Snake, you control a "snake" that continuously grows, the object being to stay alive for as long as possible. However unlike Snake, this is by default a multi player game, the object here is to stay in contention the longest. Running into yourself, another players snake, or going out of bounds ends your turn. Players are given points based on how long they last.

423719.overview:
A Sokoban inspired freeware game created by  Lorens Younes and Panagiotis Christias using C  and ReAction in 1996. In it you play the warehouse keeper and in this puzzle you must push boxes around in a warehouse, trying to get them to storage locations. The game is played on a board of squares, where each square is a floor or a wall. Some floor squares contain boxes, and some floor squares are marked as storage locations.

The player is confined to the board and may move horizontally or vertically onto empty squares (never through walls or boxes). To move a box, the player walks up to it and pushes it to the square beyond. Boxes cannot be pulled, and they cannot be pushed to squares with walls or other boxes. The number of boxes equals the number of storage locations. The puzzle is solved when all boxes are placed at storage locations.

423722.overview: A game created by Black Five SoftDesign as an open sourced game, created with ASM 68k and AMOS. Drive your Voxel car, keep it on the road and you'll go far.

423746.overview: A homebrew platform game with humans by Ventzislav Tzvetkov, from 2002.

423761.overview: An early look at a Polish, space strategy demo prepared by the well-known Deck Six group. A strategy in which the player discovers and conquers new planets and develops life on them. While colonizing the universe, he encounters other races with whom he can trade, negotiate and fight. Some Aliens are friendly, others immediately declare war. Individual races also differ in technological advancement.

423845.overview: A Czech text adventure by Jan Burian, published by Utopia Software in 1992. Apprentice, sometimes referred to under the Czech translation "The Teen", is a port and translation of the game called Trap Door 2 on the Atari 8-bit platforms (which itself was inspired by Trap Door on the ZX). Instead of typing, most commands are point and click from the menu provided. In it, we find ourselves in the role of a witch's apple. Our master, the magician Bublifukus, went to visit his acquaintance, and we were tasked with preparing a treat called kucbaba"kucbaba" in the meantime.

423854.overview:
Atoms-X is a remake of an old game called Atoms I had on the Amiga years ago. It was written by a reader of one of the Amiga magazines of the time and they gave it away on their cover disk. Something reminded me of it recently, and I had a quick search for it. It turns out there are a couple of basic clones for Linux and Android, and one or two for Amiga, but none that particularly appealed to me. So I decided to write my own version which is fully Workbench-friendly, and to include a computer opponent, something the original never had.

This version of Atoms-X includes 3 levels of difficulty for the computer players, although often the games get to a stage where even a totally random move can cause a massive chain reaction that wins the game, so don't get angry when the easiest computer opponent beats you!! The hardest level can really be a nasty opponent, making surprisingly tactical moves. Again though, sometimes it just comes down to luck...

423871.overview: In Adults Puzzle 3 you once again arrange the pile are pieces in a 5x3 grid and you get more naughty pics in this freeware game by Mak Soft Group from 1990.

423873.overview: Arrange the pile are pieces in a 5x3 grid and you get a naughty pic in this freeware game by Mak Soft Group from 1990.

423897.overview:
As a public transport lover you will love this new game. Advanced Tramway Simulator is a realistic tram simulator. The program does not impress with graphics, but surprises with a high level of realism. If you’ve ever wanted to feel like a tram conductor, here’s the perfect opportunity.

Advanced tramwaj symulator is a very realistic recreation of tram challenges. The 3D graphics appearing in the game are poor by the current standards, but the simulator of its roots derives from the earliest management games and simulators. This does not prevent the reception of the simulation. The most important thing here is a realistic representation of the tram control. In addition, the authors of Advanced Tram Simulator wet into the game of small graphic jokes.

423915.overview: A four-reel video slot\fruit machine brought to you as shareware by Gary Hunt in 1992.

423993.overview: SunMaze on Aminet brought 3D FPS Look and Walk to Amiga in 1989. This is a 3D Maze FPS game by Werner Gunther where you can walk around in the different kind of mazes with the numeric keys on your Amiga keyboard. You walk forward with the 8 key and turn either left or right with 4 or 6.

424072.overview:
Facts and figures about the Second World War abound, and Asgard Software have taken a large wodge of information and tried to make it fun and presentable by putting it in Hyperbook form.  You are presented with a menu about various aspects of the war. Choosing a subject moves you on to a screen with other topics, and you click on one to .see the next screen. 
 
WarBook was created by Eddy Morrison from Asgard Software, and is a freeware multimedia application charting the history of World War Two. Created using Gold Disk's Hyperbook, it covers the main events of the Second World War, including text files, maps and pictures.

The text is presented in a simple text reader which anyone familiar with something like More or MuchMore will have no difficulty in using. Pictures and maps are displayed at (normally) full screen size, with a click of the mouse button returning you to the main screen.

424707.overview: A Swedish language educational game for one or two players created by Göran Magnusson and published by SPAB in 1991. The game will teach you about points of interest in Europe.

425175.overview: Atris is the addictive puzzle game, embracing our universal desire to create order out of chaos.

425796.overview: An action platformer by the BitBeam Cannon team created with the help of the Scorpion Engine.

425803.overview:
Based on l'Abbaye des Morts by Locomalito
13th Century the Cathars were being expelled by the Catholic Church out of the Languedoc. Jean & Joan Raymond run to escape the crusaders, an abandoned church seems welcoming.

438277.overview:
A game inspired by Activision's game H.E.R.O. from Atari 2600/XL, C64 and Collecovision.

There is trouble in the mines! Volcanic activity has trapped numerous miners, and it is your job to save them. As Roderick Hero, you need to make your way through the dangerous mine shaft avoiding the dangerous creatures and lava, and find out where the miners are located before you run out of energy. To help on your mission, Roderick Hero has several useful types of equipment. A prop pack will allow you to hover and fly around the mine shaft and (hopefully) avoid the many dangers within. 

Your helmet features a short-range microlaser beam which can be used to destroy the bats, spiders, snakes, and other creatures you'll encounter in the mines. From time to time, your path through the mine may be blocked by stone or lava walls. You begin each mission with six sticks of dynamite, which can be used to destroy these obstacles (be careful you don't blow yourself up, though!). If you run out of dynamite, your laser beam can also be used to destroy the walls, though this will take longer and use up more energy. As the levels progress, the mine shaft will become longer and more maze-like, creatures will more frequently block the path, and lava walls and pools will appear which are dangerous to the touch.

440407.overview: A Swedish-language educational game, focused on reading comprehension and training created by Stefan Lundberg and Jonas Lundberg, both part of SweComp and published by SPAB in 1991.

440550.overview: Six programs for Swedish preschool or elementary school age children.  A rich game compilation that combines both math, coloring of pictures and reading of short words. You must also match things such as hen and egg. A very rich educational package.

443881.overview: A four player shooter from Hippy Software in 1997. Blast your best friends in this game created using AMOS!

443912.overview:
The operation of the game should be self-explanatory. When starting the game, a language selection screen appears first. Depending on which language you choose, the interface is localized and, of course, only terms in the corresponding language are queried. In addition, the key assignment of the virtual keyboard is adapted to the appropriate layout (Z and Y are swapped).

2024 Amiga game = HOMEBREW NOT RELEASED

445120.overview: In this text-only adventure you play a P.I. and the object of the game is to find and return a stolen painting. 'Adventure 1' is a proof of concept written with ADMS (Amiga Dungeon Mastering System). It should take 20-30 minutes to complete the game depending on your experience of text adventures.Available verbs: take, drop, put, eat, drink, wear, open, close, lock, unlock, examine, turn, quit, inventory, wait, save, load, restart, credits

446060.overview:
