Take on the role of space cadet Roy in this text adventure inspired by Space Quest. Adventure 2 is a text adventure written with ADMS (Amiga Dungeon Mastering System). The game makes use of these verbs:
take, drop, put, eat, wear, open, close, lock, unlock, examine, turn, blow, connect, tie, order, use, quit, inventory, wait, rub, save, load, restart, credits. Combine a verb with a noun.

446258.overview:
A freeware game by Krzysztof Matys, published with just the first four levels done in 2010. ARCTIC HUNTER 
The Santa Claus brings gifts to children all around the world. His country is the Finland, a northern land of ice where he lives. Every Christmas he must prepare new gifts for every child in the world. This Christmas he was just ready to bring the gifts to his homeland and begin to deliver them to the children but all of sudden the sky became very dark and all stars that where there just dropped on the ground in his arctic world. "Oh.." said Santa and immediately began to collect all stars the fallen upon the ground, because he knows that the Christmas Eve cannot start without the first Christmas Star! He must collect all stars and retrieve the first one which is somewhere then put them back on the sky.

446570.overview:
AQUABYSS is a sandbox game for the Amiga computer.

In AQUABYSS you may continue the protagonist's adventures from the graphic novel or choose your own path and navigate the open, vast underwater depths. Naturally, in both modes, you may trade, explore and discover new cities, upgrade your submarine, acquire new ones, develop your character, have dialogues with NPCs, complete quests, mine resources from the ocean floor, face or avoid the dangers lurking in the depths, compare your achievements with other players, or finally meet them online in the chat. This is just a foretaste of what awaits you in the underwater world of AQUABYSS!

447052.overview: A 4 player, Tron style arcade action game created by Maik Jost  of Alive Designs and released in 1992 by Softlight and Software 2000, a year after the C64 version. The game came complete with a game level editor. You can choose a large number of worlds , the number of players and so forth, then try to keep your line from crossing itself or your opponent to win.

447056.overview: Avalon is a timed, puzzle board game, a variation of Rubik's Cube. The goal of the game is to arrange an identical pattern in the second window before the time runs out. The player can move each row in the cube to the left, right, down and up. Solving the task allows uncovering one part of prize picture. The screen is divided into three parts. The bottom part shows the information (remaining time, level code). Right window shows a pattern, which must be repeated in the left window.

447229.overview: An AMOS based freeware puzzle from Grzegorz Gajkowski of Grino Studio. It allows you to rearrange the puzzle into a scene of sexual debauchery of the best kind.

448103.overview: An AMOS based Mini-Game created by Tony Kingsmill in approximately 1992. The Earth is in great danger. Aliens have stolen hundreds of washing machines and have re-programmed them to devastate our planet! You are the last hope. Using your jet propelled lazer base, you must blast them away.

448106.overview: Alan Uno\Alan 1 is a Spanish-language shareware game created by Nicolás Morenas aka Darkness and released in 1992. The game was an early attempt at a primitive AI that you could talk with and question. Is he a psychiatrist? Is he a consultant? Is he a friend? No, no and no. Alan Uno is simply an experiment. A program to laugh with friends and have a good time. An artificial intelligence program with which we can communicate in writing and it will answer us speaking in Spanish. There are some things to discover, so get to know Alan 1.

448600.overview: A freeware game from Giovanni Iacobelli and released in 2021. The goal is to run away and not get caught while searching for the key that will open the door to the next room of the basement of the castle. There are 10 levels. Written in C++ and joystick enabled.

448754.overview: Based on the original Port from Atari XLXE this sequel to the Polish game by Tukinem is a fiendishly fun puzzle game was a submission the the AmiGameJam 2024 and now being published with polish and updates by K&A+ as a two floppy set in a hard box with manual and some fun gifts. Avoid baddies, magnets and other robotic hazards to get to the spaceship that will get you farther in your quest.

448984.overview: A snake game created by Centori Software Productions and released by the infamous Courbois Software in 1990.

448993.overview:
It's a beautiful day, and the grass is getting really long. Time to clip the lawn, choose your mower and get to it, but watch out for rocks. Whenever you finish trimming the grass, you get a message, which can be random. So I played till I had them all (think I got them all). As the game has no ending.  

Every third time you lawn, you die from an epileptic fit, caused by hitting a rock. Btw, there is also "Advanced Lawnmower Simulator 2: The Revenge of King Zord!", but only for Flash it seems. This game is based on an old ZX Spectrum game released on April Fool's 1988. This one came out sometime in 1994, developed by Team 4.5 and published in Amiga Power.

448994.overview: A game released (With Zock Out) as an Amgia Fun cover disk for September of 1990 by Johannes Lipp (coding and graphics) and Holgar Kral (music/sfx). This game challenges you to fly inside the box and stay inside the box through twists and turns and difficult maneuvers.

449011.overview: The Killing Cloud: hidden game on second disk

449014.overview: A Christmas themed demo version of ATR.  ATR: All Terrain Racing is an overhead racing game from Team 17 featuring a variety of circuits including snow, mountains and more snow. The graphics are overhead view and scrolling, with a forced perspective nature. Most levels have long and short ways round, which adds a hint of navigation and strategy to the proceedings. Unlike the company’s earlier Overdrive, there is a variety of corners, rather than just 90-degree ones. A variety of power-ups and advancements are on offer. Merry Christmas!

449015.overview: The first in a duo of quiz\word games from Intellectual Software, this one released by Queue Inc in 1986. The games were created in AmigaBASIC. In them you are quizzed to help you analyze, solve, and practice analogies to improve scores on college aptitude tests.

449284.overview:
The second in a compilation of games from Markt & Technik, released in 1992. It contained the games:
JumpingJack
DigiIT
The Turn
Cul de Sac
4-Seg
Reversi
 
These compilations were sold in Europe, especially German, Austria and Switzerland.

449302.overview: Power Blast, Magic Puzzle, Rough Castle, MoveIT, Magic-Rub, Brainstorm

449435.overview: A game bundled with the 3D Construction Kit II by Andreas Smith. The objective of this first person adventure is to collect ten candles and escape. Use the mouse to click icons around the 3D window to move, click on the 3D window with the left mouse button to fire and the right mouse button to activate and collect. Click the candle icon to see how many candles you have of the ten needed.

449585.overview: A traditional game of Draughts\Checkers for Amiga for one or two players, created by Steve Hargreaves as Licenseware in 1998. It has nine levels of difficulty, the higher the difficulty the longer the computer will take to respond. The game is over when one player has lost all his pieces or is unable to move.

449645.overview:
The sequel to Colossal Adventure is an interactive fiction game with a VERB NOUN interface.

The fantasy setting takes a clear influence from Lord of the Rings. After centuries of harmony, Middle Earth has hit problems due to a cataclysmic sequence of events - a crop failure leading to animals turning violent, and then an attack from a mysterious enemy to the north. The evil Demon Lord Alagiarept is discovered to be responsible, and as such the Wizards are given a week to beat him, before Middle Earth must surrender.

You play a rookie magician with Meditation, Mysticism and Moneymaking skills. While the main war goes on, you attempt a much bolder mission - locate the four Stones-of-the-Elements and the Medallion of Life to enter Alagiarept's Dark Tower and kill him.

Your quest will take you through Beaches, Moors and Rocky Outcrops, as well as more specific locations such as the Pillar in the Desert, the Cave of the Sun-Dial and the Mills of God. Wolves, skeletal hands, sharks and octopuses must be dealt with. 
 
ADVENTURE QUEST, only available as part of the JEWELS OF DARKNESS compilation on the Amiga, enhances the original text-only incarnations released for 8-bit platforms by adding graphics, more extensive text descriptions, an extended parser that understands many more commands and other user-friendly features (e.g. multitasking, a quit back to WB option). Available as part of the Jewel of Darkness Compilation release.

449668.overview:
The game is inspired by The Hobbit, Leisure Suit Larry, Police Quest and Mission Impossible. Your mission is to find the three rings of power and destroy them.

How to play
The game makes use of these verbs: take, give, drop, put, eat, wear, open, close, lock, unlock, examine, turn, tie, order, use, quit, inventory, wait, save, load, restart, credits.

Combine a verb with a noun. 
ie: open door, take jar

You can also combine this with in, on and with.
ie: turn on light,  unlock door with key, put book on shelf, put pickle in jar

Move by typing n, e, s, or w.
 
Game created by Grindercowboy aka Quantumcodemonk in 2024 and released as freeware.

449677.overview:
The first and only game using "The Puzzle Gallery" engine, for which there were supposed to be multiple Puzzle Disks. Extremely similar in style to Are We There Yet? and The Fool's Errand, "At the Carnival" includes word searches, jigsaws, block puzzles, word squares, crosswords, jumbles, cryptograms, mazes, and more.

Each puzzle is set at and somewhat related to a different attraction at Hazard Park. There are total of 40 attractions, and 180 puzzles.  
 
The Puzzle Gallery: At The Carnival was originally developed for the Apple Macintosh in 1989. The Amiga conversion was created for Miles Computing. Also published in Amiga Future #134 (coverCD), Sept/Oct 2018, publisher was APC&TCP.

449678.overview: A shareware, four-player artillery game created by Michael Boeh and Ed Erst in 1993. Each of your opponents (up to 3!) compete to get the correct firing solution on his fellow players. With just the right charge and angle you can take them out one by one as you all take turns to be the first to get the tough shots. Artillerus is based on the old concept of angle and power, get it right and blow them up before they get you. A variety of weapons and defenses are available.  Played on stunning alien landscapes created by the computer for each match. Choose the number of rounds until a winner is declared and be the best shot on the block, the BIG SHOT!

449698.overview: A sports management game seemingly, only ever sold via mail order direct from the developer/publisher Composer Software. In it you play in a worldwide based on the real World League of American Football that was active in 1991 and 1992. Manage London against heavy hitters like the Sacramento Surge as they grind the grid-iron in search of a ten yard advance or a touchdown. Trade, set contracts and get the best players to win a true world championship and the AMOSBowl. The game was created in AMOS and sold commercially via mail order and through Shareware.

449741.overview: A freeware AMOS archery game for one or two players created by Marc Le Douarain in 1993. Hit moving targets with accuracy! Different targets move with different speed. The score when you hit a target is proportional to the speed and accuracy of the shot. To shoot if you play alone, use the left button on your mouse. If you play as player 2, you must use a joystick button while the first uses the mouse.

449744.overview: Amiga Concentration v3.3 is a shareware game created by Alan Keith, Heither Keith using AMOS and released in 1992. The object of the game is to guess a hidden five-letter word. Each time you find two matching pictures, two pieces of the word will be revealed. If two people play, you can alternate games and try to guess the word in fewer turns than your opponent.  Or you can alternate turns in the same game until one player finds a match, then that user continues as long as they continue matching pictures.

449758.overview: A 1997 AMOS based game of American Checkers (Droughts), created by Thomas Powell. A game for one or two players, with custom colored pieces available, also allowed game tracking statistics.

449775.overview: A freeware avoid it game created by Michael Mueller of Axival Software, the 2001 game was rescued and re-released in 2016. This is a vertically scrolling avoid it game. You can adjust the speed during the game F1 - F3 keys change. Would you like to save this setting then press the S key, then there is a short pause, which gives the computer some time to adjust the setting into one file to be saved in the same directory as the ASBII file is secured.

449776.overview: An unfinished blitz BASIC shareware game from Vision Software in 1993 released in the LSD Compendium Deluxe Volume. Vision Software was staffed by Paul Andrews and Rod Smith. It is a horizontally scrolling fantasy shooter, where you play a flying demon who must shoot down waves of bats, grim looking birds and other gruesome flying adversaries.

449974.overview: A freeware compilation of educational mini-games by Stuart Ashton of Dancing yak Productions, for one or two players, released in 1995. They included a number game, a quiz, yak racing, a waggler\dancer and a cheat lister. It also lists access to a personal assistant, paint and speech synthesis.

449975.overview: Awaking" makes the opening! Awaking is a quiz game such as Jeopardy, Riskant or Der grosse Preis. Pick your player 1 through 3 from a cast of characters and choose the difficulty of the question. Questions and answers are in German in this 1995 game by Frank Abbing.

449981.overview:
Blast giant wasps with a mechanical spider as at jumps.  a bionic spider (half tarantula, half machine) designed by the government in the early 19903 to ward off attacks of giant African killer wasps. Part of a class of computer-controlled robo-spiders used for defense. 
 
Giant killer wasps are headed this way and it's up to you to stop them. You're prepared, though; Equipped with a joystick controlled model A500 Arachnoid, you have the potential to knock out an entire swarm of angry insects.

But wait! Radar reports not one, but nine swarms of wasps, spaced at ten-mile intervals. To complete your mission, you'll have to blast each and every bug out of the sky, wave after wave. So grab a joystick, power up your computer, take a deep breath, and fire! You've got a serious insect problem to take care of. 
 
Created by David Wright and released as a cover disk in the December 1989 COMPUTE!'s Amiga Resource - Volume 1 Number 5 from COMPUTE! Publications.

450206.overview: Alchemy's Snakes Version 1.2 was released as shareware in 1993 by Alchemy Software Development's Richard Jones. It was also released in WorkbenchGamesVolume3 and in The AssassinsPD. Snake is a game where the more items you eat the longer you get, but the higher your score. You must avoid connecting with your own tail as this will end the game.

450243.overview: An AMOS based freeware game created by David Hobbs and released in 1991. In this one you  play  a  kid named...Adrian!  Your aim is to find the Golden Chalice which is hidden somewhere in the checkerboard desert.  To reach it you have to avoid many obstacles.

450261.overview: Contains  four  versions  of  the  old Asteroids game.  On version 1 all graphics  are  computed  rather  than drawn by an artist.  Disc contains full  documentation.   The  game  is  played  with  a  joystick  and the objective  is  to  destroy  as  many  levels of rocks as possible and to destroy  the  alien ship when it appears.  Treat yourself to a trip down memory lane or show the kids what games used to be like. A freeware game created in AMOS by Mike Widdess and released in 1991.

450262.overview:
A freeware puzzle game created by Colin Naylar with AMOS and distributed in multiple collections and by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) and The Assassins in 1993.  

Place Tiles on the Board with adjacent sides, matching colours or designs. The outer darker area of the Board may be used but point are not scored on these parts. Matching tiles on more than one side scores extra points matching on four sides scores four points in in the first instance, but next four way scores eight points, the next sixteen and so on.

450288.overview: Amos Invaders by SM Sutton is a version of the old classic Space invaders which is very well done with aliens which get faster and faster as the game progresses. The game often is found in a two pack with Creepy Crawly.

450289.overview: Released as part of The Classics Collection, Monopoly from Horbinder Singh Ghag gives the feeling of the original board game and is for up to four players. It was created using AMOS in 1992.

450290.overview: This  version  of  hangman  has  versions  for children and adults.  The children's   version   has  a  sequence  of  soldiers  marching  on  the unfortunate  prisoner,  for  each  wrong guess another soldier brings on part  of  the  gallows and the prisoner shows signs of great despair, if you  guess correctly, he jumps for joy!  I found this idea quite amusing even  if  rather  macabre,  look  out for the final sequence.  The adult version  has  different  animation  with various parts of the hanged man being added for each incorrect answer.

450352.overview: A shareware game created by Christian Hurst and published in 1991 by Kings Guild Software.

450353.overview: An AMOS based Tron Light Cycle\Worm style game released as freeware by Chris Good in 1992. In the game you avoid the light line behind your opponent but try to get them to touch your light line.

450360.overview: A Mines is a Minesweeper clone developed by Manfred Huesmann and released into the public domain in 1992.

450393.overview: An educational freeware game where the alphabet can be seen and experienced by a young user. It will automatically show the Alphabet by showing the letters in order or if a letter key is pressed it will display for that letter.

450401.overview:
A math instruction game that covers Area and Volume, Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division, Fractions and
Percent.  Future updates were planned for Trigonometry, but it is unclear if it came to pass. On loading you are presented with a menu. You must use the numbers on the keypad not the keyboard. There is speech when you complete  a  set  number  of questions.  Well produced program to help you solidify your math knowledge by Simon Jewell in 1991.

450450.overview: A 1991 freeware puzzle game created by Grzegorz Gajkowsk of Grino Studio. Sort the image parts to make a cohesive whole single picture.

450510.overview:
Algebra Plus is an introductory Algebra tutorial and practice program designed to be used in conjunction with a standard Algebra textbook or as a supplement to a classroom course. the program consists of two volumes of two disks each. Disk one contains the tutorial and practice material. Disk two contains tests and a glossary of the terms used. The program is entered through a Master Menu and provides the ability to return to any part of the program for further review and study. Each section also is entered through an index so that any material is readily accessed.  
 
Sections include:
The Real Number System
Equations in One Variable
Using Formulas
Graphing of Equations in Two Variables
Linear Equations in Two Variables
Word Problems
General Properties of Plynomials 
 
This program can be run in the Workbench.

450523.overview: A German language shareware word game for up to 6 players, created by Peter Handel in 1993. Similar to Wordle, this game presents a 5x5 grid where you must guess the word based on matching letter and letter placement. The faster you solve, the higher your points. Rounds can be set to last for 5, 16 or 20 rounds in which the word must be found. The unregistered version has 500 words, the full registered version has 1400 and also contains a word list editor.

450556.overview:
A freeware, head to head maze game for two players, created by Crain in 1993.
A game for two players in which you must reach and shoot the yellow smiley face. The player moves through a maze with obstacles in the form of red walls, which must be broken through by creating a hole of the appropriate size. Contact with any element of the environment results in the loss of a life. The game ends if one of the opponents loses all their lives or one of the players has more points after shooting down the last smiley face.

450577.overview: Amiga Castles v2.01 is a freeware workbench game released by Dirk Wachtel (aka Count Diwi) in 1994. A small strategy game for two players after the old Atari game template.

450586.overview: A shareware German-language game created in Oberon and released in 1990. You play as a student and the actions you make will help you pass or fail your grade.

450636.overview: A Polish-language educational program containing a world atlas with detailed data and the ability to edit the database. In addition to a large amount of didactic material, the player has at his disposal a set of tests that can be freely configured. The developer of the AMOS game is unknown, but it was released by Romi Soft in 1993 and Gracomm in 1994.

450743.overview:
This homebrew port of the 1977 version of Adventure is credited to only Crowther and Woods, the original authors of the PDP-10 version of the game. This homebrew port was released as freeware in 1992. Hoping to reconnect with his estranged daughters following the collapse of his marriage, in 1976 programmer and spelunker Will Crowther rigged a text parser to interact with a narrated simulation of the Bedquilt region of Kentucky's real-life Mammoth Cave system he and his wife Pat had explored and mapped together.

Starting with a faithful reproduction of geological formations he upped the gameplay potential (oh boy... rocks!) with an injection of period "Frodo Lives!" pseudofantasy tropes (including angry dwarfs and that first great video game magic word "xyzzy") and stocked the cavern complex with a series of treasures to be collected and deposited back topside.

The formula was later built and improved upon by a host of others over almost 50 (!) years now, most notably by Don Woods, but an August 2007 rediscovery of March 1977 backups of Crowther's original source code reveals how many important elements of the game's design were already present in the earliest versions.

450744.overview: A freeware Chess program for 1 or 2, created by Michael Taupitz and released in several Amiga freeware compilations, including those by Berliner Speilekiste. Version 2.0 of the game released in 1993. The playing strength of the computer opponent is quite good! From blitz chess to a tournament mode and the analysis function, all kinds of options are offered, games that have been started can be saved and misguided moves can be undone.

450775.overview: A freeware AMOS based game for one or two players created by K. Grigg in 1992. Bedsprings to action in Sea, on Earth and in Space. Avoid hazards and bounce as far as your springs will take you! Items you pick up can help you travel further.

450778.overview: A single-player freeware AMOS game created by Master Byte. Fly through the skies and let nothing get in your way, weapons hot you clear the lane. They don't pay you to come back with ammo!

450798.overview:
Released as part of the WPJ Garbage Collection in 1991, and as a Matrix Club release on disk GA04e. This game is a conversion of the BBC Micro version of Lode Runner. In the game, The Bungeling Empire has stolen a huge cache of gold from its rightful owners, and your mission is to infiltrate its treasury and recapture it. This entails progressing through 150 screens of platforms, ladders and ropes.

The Empire has sent robotic guards down to protect the gold, and contact with any of these will cost you a life. Your method of escaping them is to press fire to dig a hole in their line of movement, thus causing them to fall in briefly, allowing you to move across the gap safely. Once all the gold has been collected, a ladder allowing you to move onto the next screen is added. Completing these screens often requires forward planning and precision.

450799.overview: A version of Boulderdash with a more compact view of the mine. Created by Arto Niskanen to accept mini dash gamefiles so new mines can be quickly and easily created. Application created in ASM 68k and released as freeware in 1994. Shipped with a built-in level\game editor. Sets of 6 Adventure Mini Dash levels were widely distributed.

450801.overview:
Air Traffic Control is a shareware release from Griff Jackson in 1990. ATC is a program that simulates an air traffic regional control center, You are the controller, and you direct the planes (up to 8 at a time) to the airport. You control the planes' heading, altitude and speed. You receive points for directing the planes correctly to the airport. You also have to contend with planes departing from the same airport, and you have to make sure that the planes do not collide with each other. You also have only a limited amount of time to get the plane to the airport. You receive fewer points for a late flight, and if a flight is very late, it will run out of fuel and crash. All program input is done with the left mouse button.

ATC is SHAREWARE. If you like it, use it, and would like to promote this method of software distribution, please send a donation to the author. Registered users (those donating $15) will receive a disk containing:

- a version of the program using digital sound effects
any future upgrades
Modula-2 source code

450812.overview: A Mancala 1.19 is a shareware game created by Thorsten Koschinski in 1991. It is a Mancala game for one or two players. Mancala is a two-player strategy board game where players take turns moving counters around a board of holes to capture their opponent's pieces, trying to capture as many opponent's pieces as possible. Players take turns picking up counters from one hole and dropping them one by one into consecutive holes. Players can capture counters by reaching a certain part of the board or accumulating a certain number of counters in a hole.

450827.overview: A freeware board game for one or two players created by Kai Nickel in 1997 using C++ / MUI, it was released on Assassins CD3 and Ultimate Games '97 compilations. The 2.20 version was the version released in 1997. It is an implementation of the board game Abalone. It is played on a hexagonal board. Each player starts up with 14 marbles and the goal is to kick the enemy marbles off the board. The game is over when a player has lost 6 of his marbles. The game runs on the workbench and is localized for English or German. It requires the MUI-System 3.6 or higher be installed.

450828.overview:
A Reversi Player is a single player board game video game for Amiga OCS, created and published by Manuel Almudevar in March 1986 as freeware. You play WHITE. The mouse is used to select moves. Move the pointer onto the square on which you wish to play, and press the left button. The move is made when the button is released, so you can change your mind before letting go of the button by moving the pointer off the board. This can also be used to remove the red cursor box if you find it distracting.

The Voice option tells you when it is your move - at higher levels moves can take several minutes. This program runs at a low priority, so you can run interactive tasks (eg. an editor) with good response time, while the program is "thinking".

The board is displayed on a screen, not a window, so you can pull it down to reveal the workbench, or use the back/front gadgets.

Moves are made by placing a white piece so that it outflanks one or more black pieces. One or more black pieces must lie between the new piece and another white piece, diagonally, horizontally, or vertically. Outflanking can occur in more than one direction. The outflanked pieces are flipped, and become white. A game ends when all positions are filled, or when neither side can move. The side with the most pieces on the board at the end of a game wins.

It sometimes occurs that you do not have any legal moves. If this occurs, you must forfeit. (The program will not do this automatically for you - I find that I like to "stay" in the game, even if I cannot move!). Two commands are useful if you are learning to play. The "Moves" command shows you all of your allowed moves. The "Suggest" command suggests a good (not best) move.

Level 5 is the hardest level. The program may take several minutes to move at this level. The level can be changed during the game. Since moves in the middle of the game take longer, you may wish to start and end a game at a high level, and reduce the level when moves are taking too long. The Voice "It is your move" statements are suppressed for levels 1 and 2, since it takes longer to say them than to move. The other helpful (?) statements remain. All menus are disabled while the Busy sign is up.

Comments: The program is not fast, but plays a reasonable game. It does not always start off intelligently. The strongest point seems to be the endgame (so don't get too optimistic too early!). There is a slight randomization in its evaluation function, so it will not always make the same response to the same sequence of moves.

451360.overview:
Compilation from Ozi Soft and released in 1990, it includes the following titles: 

* Ball Raider II
* Championship Othello
* Diablo
* Space Baller
* Swooper
* Zitrax

451361.overview:
Luca Carminati of LC-Games, has released all of his Amiga games that he coded in the years 1995/1998.  

There's a space shooter, Croins, which looks a little bit like a classic Asteroids game, a Worms/Snake like Arcade game, Hyper Viper with lots of levels, collectable fruit and deadly skulls, Kangy, a family friendly platformer with a nice little soundtrack, Marietto a mario-esque popping arcade game, and finally Slalom Speciale, a Skiing simulator for those of you who enjoy a bit of winter sports.

451450.overview:
A one or two player shareware Majong game from Danny Y. Wong in 1995. Mah Jong is an ancient Chinese game that consists of 144 tiles, the 144 tiles are broken down into the following 4 groups:
Circles: 36 tiles
Bamboos: 36 tiles
Characters: 36 tiles
Words: 28 tiles
Flowers: 8 tiles
Match up all your tiles in a three tile run sequence or 3 or 4 of a king before all 144 tiles have been taken from the deck or someone else wins. The player who starts the round receives 14 random tiles and the rest get 13.

451455.overview: Amiga Borders is the (German) implementation of the famous “Kästchen Ziehn” or cheese boxes board game - one of the most sensible uses for squared paper that I know! The aim here is to get the most squares filled in, and more than your human or computer opponent. Each board is filled with dots on a grid. Each turn a human or computer draw a line between points. If 3 of the lines are filled, the next person can close the block and score a point for themselves. If you enclose a block you get another chance to put down a line. Late in the game this can lead to a train of blocks being filled. The most filled at the end wins! You can also design these patterns yourself using an included editor.

451457.overview: A shareware management game created by Roland Richter in 1993. Also published on Time-Disk #171: Askalon with Cantrix. In the game you race to become the king, through land and resource management, training of trades and warriors. You start in the year 483 and get started in creating a kingdom to rule the continent.

451458.overview: Part of a wide-ranging series of German-language freeware games and utilities by Andreas Sauer (The AS in AS Soccer), this one a soccer management game where you trade and train the best players to win the tournament sportsball championship!

451459.overview: A reworking of the classic asteroids game. Manoevre your spacecraft to avoid the asteroids. Fire at them to destroy them, but steer clear of the debris! Control is either by keyboard or by joystick. Try to destroy the asteroids and avoid the flying saucers. Simple but addictive game play throughout. A shareware game from Sinister Developments in 1993. Language options for English, French, German, Italian and Spanish.

451465.overview:
A Paper-doll game for changing clothes. Kiss is based on a popular Japanese game called 'Kisekae' that translates
to "changing clothes".  The game involves manipulating and overlaying items of clothing over the bodies of popular Japanese anime characters. This game is not restricted to just changing clothes on people either. Kiss data is available for battleships and mecha too. 

Three sets have been included in this archive - sallyez.lzh, mogami.lzh and asukakis.lzh. These should be unarchived into separate directories.

This program is thanks to all the other Amiga programmers out there that have created software to make the Amiga such an excellent platform and fun computer.  It is ShareWare game created by Victor Ng-Thow-Hing.

451466.overview: A freeware, single play adaptation of Asteroids created by Rico Mariani in December of 1987 as a Christmas gift to the Amiga community. It comes with simple instructions on how to edit the asteroids pictures so you can make your own Asteroid themed releases. At least one game of this type was made by substituting faces for the game's asteroid images.

451467.overview: A freeware memory game for up to 8 players created by Tis Vuegen in 1994.

451468.overview:
First Amiga implementation of a widespread combination logic and skill game (Klack). Balls are thrown into a standing  upright game board and then fall to different heights (based on the logic of the locking rockers) - thereby changing how the next ball will flor. Determine where to drop and how to arrange them for the best score... For 1 or 2 players.
Limited demo version (only two different game options of the game; the full version currently contains: 13).
Shareware from Detlef Schäfer in 1994.

451470.overview:
A patience style solitaire game created by Frank Niessen (also spelled Frank Nießen) and released by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) in 1994. A patience game with two deck's of cards. The object of the game is to build a stack of cards in the same suit from King to Ace, and remove the stack from the table to the stacks above. When all eight stacks have been built and removed, you have won the game. 

A more challenging version of this is t leave all 8 stacks on the table until done, instead of removing those that are complete to the stacks above. Needs OS2.0, PAL interlace screen, and it would be nice to have a three-button-mouse. This is version 1.1. Includes source in C.

451473.overview:
A shareware scrabble game for up to four players created by Martin Powell and published in 1994. Welcome to Martin Powell's AMIGA SCRABBLE. Scrabble is a game for 2, 3 or 4 human players.  Play consists of forming interlocking words, crossword fashion, on the scrabble board, using letter tiles with various score values.

Each player competes for the highest score by using his tiles in combinations and locations that take best advantage of letter values and premium squares on the board. An up to the minute scoresheet can be seen by licking on the Score icon. Any words listed in a standard dictionary are permitted,except those spelt with an initial capital letter, abbreviations,
prefixes and suffixes and words requiring apostrophes or hyphens. Save and load previous game is disabled in unregistered versions.

451474.overview: A freeware puzzle and logic game created by Adam Levin-Delson for a single player and released in 1995. The game functions as the original Black Box board game. It was published in several PD and shareware compilations, including Assassins G247 CD3. in this version you can set the amount of Atoms in the chamber and the size of the chamber for difficulty. The player must deduce the location of the hidden atoms by shooting rays into the box and seeing where it is reflected out of the chamber.

451475.overview: A shareware game for one or two players released in 1990 by Volker Majewski. In AlienForce you have to drive a small robot through an "enemy" spaceship to collect liquor bottles. Of course there are a few obstacles like "enemy" robots, code card doors, projectors, different floor coverings... A game that can easily hold its own against a commercial game. With level editor and saveable high score!

451476.overview: A freeware board game for up to 4 players created by Henry Konig in GFA BASIC in 1991. A modernized digital adaptation of the ancient Indian board game Pachisi.

451477.overview: Aliens Lair is a 1-2 player vertically scrolling space shooter for the Amiga using SEUCK. It was developed and released by Frank Otto in 1994.

451488.overview:
A freeware slot\fruit machine program made by Tim Quigley of Madsoft Inc in 1997 using Blitz BASIC, with a sequel released the next year. It's a fruit machine, nuff said. Oh yeah, to quit press escape or click on the tiny Q gadget in the top left hand corner.

451491.overview:
How do you play volleyball Without hands? With your head, of course! Arcade Volleyball" is a one- or two-player arcade-style game with colorful graphics, smooth animation, and sound. You control a high-jumping, if short of stature, expert volleyball player. It won't be long before you'll be executing topnotch serves, sets, and spikes.

Arcade Volleyball is written in Lattice C 5.0, but you don't need Lattice C to run the program. Simply boot your computer with the Resource Disk, double-click the disk Icon, open the Volleyball drawer that looks like a folder, and then double-click the icon labeled Arcade Volleyball. To copy the program to another disk, such as a hard disk, you must copy the entire Volleyball folder, not just the program file.

Arcade Volleyball uses stereo sound. If you don't have both the left and right Amiga audio channels connected to an audio output device, you will not be able to hear all of the game's sounds. Arcade Volleyball sounds best when your Amiga is connected to a stereo amplifier or a stereo monitor. 

Amiga version by Rhett Anderson, Tim Midkiff, and Randy Thompson and released as a coverdisk in COMPUTE!'s Amiga Resource - Volume 1 Number 3 (1989-08) by COMPUTE! Publications.

451496.overview: In an atomic lattice you have to search for atoms. To do this, electron beams are sent through, whose exit point can be used to deduce the positions of the atoms, if you can. A tricky task! A black box style game by author: Norbert Ossenkopp in 1991.

451497.overview: A freeware management game by Michael Grimm, created in 1992 where you must manage the auto shop business and become the most successful.

451498.overview: A small, freeware, single player guessing game, created with AMOS by Uwe Hartel in 1996.

451505.overview: A 1994 freeware quiz game created by Siegfried Hundt for Rosensoft. Offering multiple choice fun, in the German language. Version 1.9 was released in 1994. The game has been created in AMOS.

451510.overview: An AMOS based freeware game from Jesse McClusky from 1994. As the original PAL version by John Grivin wouldn't fully work on our NTSC machines I wasforced to make my own. So my code is all original, even if the ideas are not. This new version of my game is easily 5 to 10x faster than Atoms 2 and has varying levels of AI opponents. Additionally, it has an interlaced mode quadrupling the number of squares available. And if blocks are on, you can have quadruple the number of those too, just to keep an even distribution. And the mouse-adjustment issue from version 2 is now fixed. And from 2 to 5 can play and you can set how many of these are computer players, even creating a demo mode if you like.

451629.overview: A freeware minesweeper game created by Jean-Marc Gigandet in Blitz BASIC with version 1.05 released in 2000.

451755.overview: Amiga Dice-O is a Yahtzee style, shareware dice game where you roll dice and try to get 3 and 4 of a kind in the style of a poker hand, Full House, Low and High Straight, collections of one through six and the Dice-O is basically Yahtzee, 6 of a kind. The game automatically keeps score for you, so that is a big help over the board game version. The game was created by Martin Bansey and released as Shareware in 1993. Released in Assassin 216 and CD LSD Compendium Deluxe 2.

451761.overview: An AMOS based shareware action game created by Chris Hurst of Kings Guild Software and released in 1991. Your robot is trapped in a strange world which is unstable.  To escape the robot must fit 150 micro-chips into his teleporter.  The chips appear randomly along with bombs and holes. There's also a robotic ghost to avoid.

451762.overview: The Adventure Construction Kit (ACK), not to be confused with Adventure Construction Set (ACS) from Electronic arts. This is a freeware adventure game creator developed by Robert Muller and published as freeware in 1993. It is a German language application.

451982.overview: A 1993 freeware game created by Janusz Urbanowicz and unleashed on the world in 1993. Version 1.03 was distributed with Imazine #3 that year. This is an avoid-it action game where you must plot your moves to keep one step away from the evil Daleks. If they catch you they will EX TER MIN ATE you.

452096.overview: A freeware duel for two players. In this two player game each player controls an artillery gun set in a mountain landscape with the goal of destroying the other player. Players in this version fire on each other a the same time, so you need to get your settings in fast. The barrel angle and powder level can be set in order to control the direction and distance of the shot. When deciding on your shot, you will need to take the current conditions into account, which includes wind speed/direction and any mountains that may get in your way. Successfully destroying your opponents gun will earn you a point, and the first player to reach the set number of points wins the game.

452118.overview: A single player, freeware game by Rick GIles, inspired by the game The Adventures of Robin Hood for the Atari 800xl. This game revolved around picking up bags of silver, shooting the sherrifs men and getting a life-enhancing kiss from Maid Marian.

452220.overview: A freeware puzzle game by Olivier Lux, 1.1 was released in 1998. Unscramble the picture puzzle into the correct image. Set the image and piece size and even upload additional high res pictures.

452306.overview: A freeware puzzle game for one user created by Gareth Murfin who fashioned himself the head of Alpha Software in 1997. Touted as a complex game of intrigue and mystery, but in reality it is a guessing game. Guess the number the computer determined. It will let you know if you need to guess higher or lower. The game was made specifically for entry into the Amiga Format readers game section!

452390.overview: A "Rocks and Diamonds" variant of the Boulder Dash game created by Artsoft Entertainment in 1991. Arcade style game for color with stereo sounds. A game like "Boulderdash" or "Emerald Mine" Included are 5 levels known from the games "Boulderdash". Comes with full source code and the Zaphod level editor. Levels created for the Unix versions can be used on the Amiga version. You can change level by clicking on the blue rocks at the bottom of the screen. Classic mines like Snake Bite, BD2K3 and Walpurgis Gardens can all be found for the Amiga.

452467.overview:
This is a powerful and accurate lawn mowing simulation. Choose from several different machines and 'go get that grass'! This freeware game was released in 1997 by the aptly named Unsatisfactory Software, based on an April Fool's joke from 1988.  In the game you can select the mower of your choice.

452486.overview:
The Aliens are Coming is a 1-player fixed screen shooter for the Commodore Amiga.

It bares resemblance to games like Galxian and Galaga. It was developed by WeatherMine Software and released into the public domain in 1992.

452491.overview:
Angband is a single-player, text-based, dungeon simulation derived from the game Moria, an enhancement of the old unix game Rogue. It is often described as a "roguelike" game because the look and feel of the game is still quite similar to Rogue.

Angband features many enhancements over Moria: unique foes, artifacts, monster pits and vaults to name a few. Many of these new creatures and objects are drawn from the writings of J.R.R Tolkien, although some of the monsters come straight from classical mythology, Dungeons & Dragons, Rolemaster, or the minds of the orginal Angband coders.

The ultimate goal of the game is to develop a character strong enough to defeat Morgoth, who lurks around dungeon level 100. Upon doing so, you will receive the exalted status of "winner" and your character may retire.

Angband is a reference to Morgoth's "prison of iron."

452646.overview: An Emerald Mines\Boulderdash style game created with the Emerald Mine Editor by The Bullfrog and released by the Emerald Mines Club of Australia in 1992. This version pulls from the C64 game of the same name and supports only one player. Otherwise it appears to follow normal Emerald Mines rules, collect the gems and avoid being crushed or caught by baddies.

452728.overview: A freeware 2-player game created by Hanno Behrens. It's an avoid it game, don't let anything touch you, maneuver to make robots crash into each other for added times. Beat you highest move count and run the high scores if you are able.

454238.overview: Anguish is the spiritual sequel to Agony for AGA Amigas.

454347.overview: This game is based on Police Quest 1, a game created and published by Sierra On-Line in 1987. But here the roles are switched and you play as Jessie Bains, the antagonist, a drug dealer and a card shark with the intention to take control of the drug trafficking in the city of Lytton.

454477.overview: Amanda's Alphabet Jigsaw Jumble is an Educational game created and published by Rush Software in Oceania. Un-jumble the pictures to see the word that corresponds to the letter you chose. Learn while you play!

454512.overview:

The Polish author Jakub Madej released the source code of the general public and Sun68 fixed the Amiga E source to resolve some lingering errors. The game is primarily intended for future versions and to learn the AmigaE language. The goal is to collect all the diamonds (4/level) to get into the next level. Press the arrow keys High (Up), down, right (right) and left (Lefth).
Use the button "Q" or "ESC" for the end of the game. Touch the "R" button in the game for a new beginning (reload) of a level. There are 15 levels + 35 master levels.

454534.overview: Adventure 2 Remake' is a game written with Scala MM400, and it's a point and click version of the text adventure 'Adventure 2'

457145.overview:
The advanced version of the other Junior Reading package utilises the same format as the 4/5 version with the addition of a few new elements.

Where the other acts as a primer, each letter sounds and shapes, this one goes much further. Now the user is required to learn more complicated letter sounds and read and spell more complicated words.

For the most part this version is almost identical to its younger brother and they even share the same manual. The games take on an almost identical format, although the questions are much tougher. This means that if your child genius speeds through that package they won't feel out of place using this one.

All the extras are still there, including Paint Pot which is an easy-to-use art package. The amount of tools available depends on the level the application is set to, initially there is only a few line tools, eraser and a box icon to choose from. Cut and paste tools, a symmetry feature and a fill tool can be added.

Again, the package goes into great detail while being easy to use and providing a liberal smattering of games to keep minds with otherwise short attention spans interested. Despite its ease-of-use, it is essential to keep an adult on hand to help out with the trickier puzzles and the disk swapping between programs as the disk labelling could prove a little confusing for younger children.

Equally as good as the 4/5 version, it is unmatched in its field. The variety of problems to solve and the various games and extra programs make this package extremely absorbing.

Parents need not to worry about being shown up either when it comes to using the machine as there is an extremely useful on-line help system. The perfect way to prepare kids for first year education.

It's a story meant to unfold step by step and it is intended to work like this.

461852.overview:
Playing Amiga Master Mind is very simple: after loading the program, the game's start screen appears after just a few seconds. You can read a summary of the basic Master Mind rules—which are likely familiar to almost everyone—via the "Instructions" option in the "Options" menu. To start a game, simply select the "Start Game" menu option. The computer will ask you to select the number of players from the "Players" menu; if playing with two people, after entering the players' names, the Codemaker (the person setting the sequence to be guessed) must enter the combination by clicking on the colored pegs and, once they have had a chance to note it down, can begin the game. 
 
If, however, there is only one player, the computer takes on the role of the code-maker, while the player acts as the code-breaker (the one who must guess the sequence).

Combinations must consist exclusively of five pegs of different colors. Closeness to the solution is indicated to the code-breaker by the standard black and white pegs placed next to each attempt, as well as by a colored bar in the bottom-right corner that increases or decreases based on the number of black and white pegs. Once the 15 available attempts are exhausted, the exact sequence is revealed; otherwise, if the code-breaker guesses correctly and the number of attempts beats the previous record, their name is recorded in the High Score box.

Published in the AmigaMagazine OnDisk #7.

462803.overview: The player's task is to collect the required number of diamonds within a specified time and reach the exit. During the journey, you must collect sticks of dynamite to blow up walls or stones blocking the way. Be careful not to destroy any diamonds in the process, as they may be counted one by one. 472741.overview: You play as Node, sent to investigate the source of a recent monster infestation in the Crystal Mine

475116.overview: Amiga Man is a Mega Man/Rockman style platform game developed and released by Mainake Project and placed 4th in the Posadas 2026 Homebrew Games competition.

475118.overview: Al-Mexia is a Spanish-language text adventure with graphics developed and released by Custom Real Amigas Never Emulated and placed 6th in the Posadas 2026 Wild competition.

477655.overview: Astronaut Jet Pac is a retro arcade game for Amiga computers, inspired by the classic Jet Pac known from the ZX Spectrum era.

479840.overview:
A cozy arrow puzzle game for the Commodore Amiga.
Sit back, enjoy the chiptunes and clear the board one arrow at a time.
ARROWS is a cozy minimalist logic game about finding the right order. Every arrow can only leave the board in the direction of its arrowhead. Take your time, follow the paths and discover which arrow is ready to move next.
The first levels offer a gentle introduction, while later boards gradually become more interwoven and invite you to look a little closer. There is no time limit, so you can solve every puzzle at your own pace.

480056.overview:
This is a work-in-progress demo of my port of 'Sonic The Hedgehog' from the Sega Megadrive to the Commodore Amiga 1200. The port is entitled 'Aonic'.
It is directly based on the original code. Specifically, the disassembly published by the Sonic Retro team. As such, it plays identically, although the rendering has been heavily optimized and rewritten for the Amiga. Visually, there are necessary and obvious differences. This demo is the first Act of Green Hill Zone only. But architecturally I am scaling up to deliver the complete game. The major challenge isn't converting the code, but ensuring the engine is performant on a different architecture. Around 95% of the time spent on Aonic has been devising optimisations and rearchitecting the game to run at an acceptable frame-rate.

480153.overview: A native AmigaOS 68k port of Grand Theft Auto (1997), targeting classic hardware — 68020 and up, AGA or RTG. Not PiStorm, not Vampire, not Emu68.

480424.overview:
Amiga Rescue is a new retro-style puzzle game for the Commodore Amiga, inspired by the machine we still love repairing and upgrading decades later.

Across 50 levels, you'll work your way through a series of faulty Amigas, restoring broken circuit-board traces and getting each machine running again.

The rules are simple: click the circuit pieces to rotate them and create a complete path across the board. But as the repairs become more complicated, you'll also need to deal with diodes that only allow current to flow in one direction and those old Amiga favourites, leaky capacitors.

481033.overview:
A full-blooded tennis game for the Amiga 1200, in 256 colours.
Step onto the court behind the baseline and play tennis the way the 16-bit classics promised: fast rallies, big serves, desperate lobs and an umpire who sees everything, except when he doesn't. Ace of Matchball is a new AGA game from Fliegeralarm Games, written for a stock A1200 with a hard drive and 2 MB of Fast RAM.

481050.overview: Amiga 15 Puzzle is a retro adaptation of the classic 15 Puzzle, bringing this simple but addictive puzzle game to the Amiga 500.The objective is simple: move the numbered tiles around the board and arrange them in the correct order, using the single empty space to slide the pieces into position.

481235.overview: An isometric helicopter action game for the Amiga 1200, in the spirit of Desert Strike.

481304.overview: The disk is damaged. Can you recover it? X-Sector is a new puzzle game for the Amiga.

481484.overview: Galaga for the Amiga 500: a port of the 1981 arcade game, written in 68000 assembly for a stock A500 (OCS, 512 KB of chip RAM, Kickstart 1.3, PAL).

481642.overview:
An unofficial Amiga port of the 1994 Macintosh Alone in the Dark 1.0 by Infogrames and Interplay. Explore the mansion of Derceto as Edward Carnby or Emily Hartwood, solving puzzles and surviving its creatures.

The port runs the original 68k game code with an Amiga implementation of the Macintosh services it uses. Graphics use AGA bitplanes; music and effects use Paula. The game runs through the ending and returns to the title sequence. See the coverage and limits and open work for the remaining investigations.

481669.overview: A horizontal space-opera shooter for the Amiga A500 / OCS, combining classic arcade combat, manga-style storytelling and a mysterious synthwave soundtrack.

481708.overview:
Get ready for a whole new sporting challenge on your Commodore Amiga!

AmiSports is a colourful 3D sports collection featuring 10 different sporting events, customisable characters, computer opponents and local multiplayer.

Built from the ground up using the Ami3D engine, AmiSports brings a fun, accessible sports-party experience to classic Amiga hardware.

481723.overview: Ash is a platformer for the Commodore Amiga 500, built with its own custom engine.

481796.overview:
Back in 1992, Ocean released their video game tie-in The Addams Family across multiple platforms, including the Amiga. But, alas, when the Amiga version was compared to its 16-bit brethren, one thing was noticeably missing — the backgrounds!

Well, no more!

I'm pleased to present this enhanced edition of The Addams Family for OCS and AGA Amigas, now with restored backgrounds!

481801.overview: A demake of Super Hexagon on the Amiga, heavily inspired by the original game. Avoid the walls, and try not to blink.

481848.overview:
Original game: Warren Robinett, Atari 2600, 1980.
The original 2600 game logic runs unchanged underneath, so the game plays exactly like the original: same rooms, same dragons, same bat, same secrets.

482023.overview:
ALCON comes to the Amiga

Take flight in this Amiga transcode of Alcon, also known as Slap Fight, the classic vertically scrolling arcade shoot ’em up.

Pilot your fighter through enemy territory, dodge incoming fire, and blast through waves of opposition. Collect stars and select upgrades to build your ship’s firepower as you chase a higher score.

482172.overview: One case. One order. A country that must not see you.

482879.overview: Watch as the CPU sends signals to Agnus, Denise, Gary and Paula, then repeat the sequence by clicking the chips in the same order. Each round adds one more step. Click the wrong chip and the Amiga crashes.
